Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered the Petrol Relief Scheme following a rise in petrol prices after the US-Iran war, offering eligible motorcycle, Qingqi rickshaw and small-car owners a discount of Rs100 per litre on petrol.

Under the scheme, motorcycle and Qingqi rickshaw owners can receive the discount on up to 20 litres of petrol per month, while owners of vehicles with engines up to 800cc are eligible for discounted petrol of up to 30 litres per month.

Applicants can register by sending an SMS to 9771 containing the following information:

REG, CNIC number, vehicle registration number, first word of the province name and vehicle registration date.

Once registration is complete, applicants will receive a confirmation message on their mobile phones.

Before visiting a petrol station, registered applicants must sendTOKto 9771 to receive a token number by SMS.

The token number must be presented at the petrol station to claim the discounted petrol. A confirmation message will be sent once the transaction is completed

title: Pakistan considers private investment in 4 major highway projects
author: Noman Awan
summary: Pakistan considers private investment in 4 major highway projects
content:
Pakistan is considering developing four major road infrastructure projects through public-private partnerships (PPPs) as the government seeks to increase private investment and reduce the National Highway Authority’s (NHA) reliance on federal funding.

Federal Minister for Communications Abdul Aleem Khan and Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation Muhammad Ali co-chaired a meeting in Islamabad to discuss the proposals, involving the NHA, the Privatisation Commission and the Public Private Partnership Authority (P3A).

Officials reviewed the financial feasibility and commercial potential of the proposed projects, including a 169km section of the M-10 Motorway and a motorway linking Mansehra, Naran, Jhal Khand and Chilas, with a proposed connection towards the Chinese border.

The meeting also considered the proposed Guru Nanak Expressway, which the minister for communication said could support religious tourism for the Sikh community, and an extension of the Murree Expressway to Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) to promote tourism and trade.

Aleem Khan directed NHA officials to prepare business plans and identify projects suitable for private-sector investment.

He cited the Sialkot-Kharian Motorway (M-12), which is being developed under a public-private partnership, as an example of the model being pursued.

The minister said he wanted to transform the NHA into a financially self-sustaining organisation with a value of between 500 billion and 1 trillion Pakistani rupees, reducing its dependence on the government’s Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP).

Prime Minister’s Adviser Mohammad Ali pledged support from the Privatisation Commission and P3A to assess the proposals.

Officials agreed to complete preliminary technical work and meet again within a week to review their findings.

The discussions form part of the government’s efforts to attract private investment into transport infrastructure while improving the financial sustainability of the NHA.

title: Israel detains US congressional candidate at West Bank olive harvest
author: AFP
summary: Israel detains US congressional candidate at West Bank olive harvest
content:
RAMALLAH, PALESTINE: Israeli forces on Wednesday briefly detained a US congressional candidate as he joined activists supporting Palestinians harvesting olives in the face of threats by extremist settlers.

Brad Lander, a left-wing Democrat who is expected to easily win a House seat in New York City on November 3, posted on social media that he was detained along with a group of rabbis and volunteers as they harvested olives west of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank.

“The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know,” Lander wrote on X.

He later wrote that he was released on account of his prominence, adding that “Palestinians face far worse consequences every day”.

The Israeli foreign ministry lashed out at Lander over what it called a “calculated political stunt”, and said he had ignored guidance to coordinate with Israeli authorities.

“This was not about harvesting olives. It was about harvesting headlines,” it said.

The Israeli military said that the Palestinian landowner had not requested permission to conduct the harvest.

“This coordination is necessary to ensure the security of the area and maintain public order,” it said, pointing to the “security risk of an uncoordinated harvest” near an Israeli settlement.

Israel has faced growing international criticism over violence during the harvest, with rights groups documenting multiple attacks and other disruptions each day by settlers against Palestinians.

Israel on Monday announced it had made several arrests after settlers beat up a US photojournalist covering the incidents and a French mayor who had come for the olive season.

The violence comes in the final days before Israeli elections in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has sought to shore up his right-wing base, which is staunchly pro-settlement.

Israel has come under growing fire within the United States, traditionally its top ally.

Lander, who is Jewish, is a close ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, an outspoken critic of Israeli policies.

In a party primary in June, Lander ousted the sitting congressman, Dan Goldman, one of a dwindling number of Democrats who support Israel.

title: Business Community Appreciates EXIM Bank Scheme
author: Noman Awan
summary: Business Community Appreciates EXIM Bank Scheme
content:
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan on Wednesday chaired a consultative meeting with leading exporters, industrialists and representatives of the business community to address exporters’ concerns, improve industrial competitiveness and accelerate Pakistan’s export growth.

Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry joined virtually, while Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Commerce and Industries Rana Ihsaan Afzal Khan, secretaries of concerned ministries and senior officials from relevant departments attended the meeting.

Business representatives participated both virtually and in person, said a news release.

Jam Kamal emphasised the need to diversify Pakistan’s export basket, promote value-added products, explore new international markets and remove structural barriers affecting exporters. He acknowledged challenges arising from rising energy prices, transportation and freight costs, taxation and changing global trade conditions.

The minister said the government was engaging directly with industry stakeholders to identify practical solutions through coordinated efforts involving relevant ministries and regulatory authorities.

Bilal Azhar actively facilitated the discussions, inviting representatives from different export sectors to present their concerns and encouraging officials to respond to specific issues.

He stressed the importance of documenting exporters’ problems, obtaining departmental responses and developing actionable recommendations rather than limiting the exercise to general discussions.

During the meeting, business representatives appreciated the EXIM Bank scheme for exporters, describing it as a positive initiative to improve access to export financing and support businesses seeking to expand internationally.

Industry representatives highlighted concerns regarding energy costs, the captive power gas levy, provincial infrastructure levies and rising production expenses. Petroleum Division officials provided clarifications on the gas levy mechanism.

Exporters also discussed international shipping delays, port facilitation, tax refunds and banking regulations, proposing greater flexibility in payment settlement periods due to disruptions in global logistics.

Participants recommended studying markets where Bangladesh and India enjoy preferential trade advantages and exploring improved bilateral trade arrangements to strengthen Pakistan’s export competitiveness.

Representatives of the meat and livestock sector highlighted challenges relating to foot-and-mouth disease, international sanitary requirements, border restrictions and access to Gulf markets.

Responding, Jam Kamal informed participants that Prime Minister was personally taking a keen interest in livestock development, including disease control, investment, improved breeding and value-added exports. The meeting was also informed of plans for a dedicated, private-sector-led livestock board.

Mineral exporters raised concerns regarding restrictions on mining explosives and withholding taxes, while Qaiser Saleem Shabbir (CEO), representing the surgical instruments sector, emphasised the need for technological advancement, skilled human resources, industrial investment and modernisation to enhance Pakistan’s export competitiveness.

FBR officials briefed participants on measures to improve tax refund processing and digital invoicing, while exporters highlighted difficulties relating to outstanding refunds, business visas and international compliance requirements.

Concluding the meeting, Jam Kamal said that the Ministry of Commerce would consolidate sector-specific and cross-cutting issues and seek responses from concerned ministries to develop practical recommendations for the Prime Minister’s consideration.

Bilal Azhar also emphasised that the issues raised by exporters would be compiled systematically and reviewed with the relevant departments during the next consultation.

The minister thanked business leaders and government officials for their constructive participation.

He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sustained public-private engagement, export diversification, industrial growth and strengthening Pakistan’s competitiveness in international markets.

title: Sisi says Egypt to ‘defend Saudi territory’ and will not attack Yemen
author: AFP
summary: Sisi says Egypt to ‘defend Saudi territory’ and will not attack Yemen
content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo’s proposed military support for Riyadh was to “defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen,” according to a statement from his office.

At a government event titled Egypt Forum 2026, Sisi said the “objective is to defend the kingdom’s lands and borders, as well as those of any other Arab state, should it be requested of Egypt,” his spokesman said in a statement.

Sisi on Saturday had asked parliament to authorise support for Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis, “if requested”.

The parliament, which is stacked with supporters of the president, has since held two rare secret sessions, before postponing deliberations until next week.

Following the morning event where Sisi made the speech, which was reported on a delay, a high-level Egyptian delegation visited Riyadh, the kingdom’s state news agency reported.

Egypt’s top diplomat Badr Abdelatty and spy chief Hassan Rashad delivered a letter from Sisi to Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi press agency said.

The contents of the message were not reported.

In recent weeks, Ansar Allah Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have reached an unprecedented scale, forcing Riyadh to shut its main airport and postpone a major investment conference.

A Houthi maritime blockade is also threatening oil exports from the kingdom, the world’s biggest crude exporter.

Saudi Arabia has since rallied a show of support from its allies. French President Emmanuel Macron, on a surprise ‘solidarity’ visit to the kingdom Wednesday said French troops would help shield the key oil terminal of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

The day before, the UK government announced it would deploy British fighter jets to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks.

A handful of dissenting voices within Egypt’s parliament have demanded “specific objectives and clear information” on any possible deployment and an assessment of the “potential risks to the lives of our soldiers”.

Direct military involvement is unpopular in the Arab world’s most populous nation, while memories of its last disastrous deployment in Yemen, in the 1960s when thousands of soldiers were killed fighting in the North Yemen civil war, remain alive.

That mission, under President Gamal Abdel Nasser, was later compared to the US war in Vietnam.

Riyadh is one of Cairo’s strongest allies, and a key financial backer of Sisi’s administration since the former army chief ousted Islamist president Mohammed Morsi in 2013.

In his speech on Saturday, Sisi said it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by as Riyadh’s security and stability were threatened, after the unconditional support the kingdom gave Egypt in the early days of his administration.

Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen in 2015, contributing naval and air forces and deploying warships to the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait.

But over the past decade, it has adopted an increasingly conservative foreign policy, prioritising its own national security.

It has positioned itself as a regional mediator with channels open across conflict lines, including with Hamas, Israel and Iran.

Again on Wednesday, Foreign Minister Abdelatty said Egypt’s foreign policy was defined by “wisdom and strategic balance”.

This week, Abdelatty has been in contact with Iran’s top diplomat Abbas Araghchi, who has said that Egypt’s potential involvement would make the situation “more difficult”.

“Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict,” Araghchi said in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday.

Throughout this year, as its Gulf allies have come under attack in the war between Iran and the US, Cairo has repeatedly preached caution.

The Arab world’s largest military did not issue a response even when its own Damietta port was struck by an unidentified drone in July.

It has not joined the Mecca defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August, which experts said was in order to maintain its strategic autonomy.

Besides its close alliance with the kingdom, Egypt also has its own economic woes to consider.

Along with Saudi Arabia, Egypt is hardest hit by disruptions through Bab al-Mandab, the southern gateway to its Suez Canal, revenues from which have not recovered since Houthi attacks began in 2023.

title: Breaking down Caitlin Clark and Cookie Monster’s role in the evolution of today’s brand narrative
author: Zaeem Basir
summary: Breaking down Caitlin Clark and Cookie Monster’s role in the evolution of today’s brand narrative
content:
Professional sports marketing has been undergoing a major transformation in recent years with athletes becoming increasingly important off the playing field, creating valuable ties with existing fans and turning casual viewers into new consumers.

Clark, who is known by even the most novice of sports fans for her 10,000-point career milestone and court awareness, has a love of baking as a secret side interest that her beloved core audience will undoubtedly appreciate.

The story alleviates the divide concerning superior sporting achievements and relaxed house residing by giving a globe their audiences relate to.

The cross-industry implementation, from a strategic marketing standpoint, is a great example of modern storytelling. Today’s modern audiences- especially the younger, digital native demographic – are looking for authenticity in their brand partnerships.

Instead of putting the athlete in a stereotypical gym environment, juxtaposing them with pop culture icons that everyone loves creates unforgettable, viral content that appeals to both pop culture fans and sports fans alike.

title: Kuwait court jails municipal employee, Indian for 7 Years
author: Noman Awan
summary: Kuwait court jails municipal employee, Indian for 7 Years
content:
A criminal court in Kuwait has sentenced a municipal employee and an Indian national to seven years in prison over their alleged involvement in a network accused of smuggling subsidized diesel out of the country and selling it abroad.

Four other Indian defendants were each sentenced to one month in prison, while a customs officer, a Ministry of Interior sergeant and an Egyptian marketing manager were acquitted.

The case involves allegations of customs forgery, smuggling subsidized diesel out of Kuwait and reselling it abroad after purchasing the fuel from the relevant authorities.

According to the charges, the first three defendants allegedly helped an unidentified individual forge a customs declaration to complete clearance procedures and facilitate the shipment of diesel outside the country.

Three other defendants were accused of assisting the alleged operation by preparing containers and filling them with diesel for export and resale abroad.

Another defendant was accused of participating in the alleged forgery, smuggling and sale of the fuel. The municipal employee, a public servant, was charged with falsifying official documents, including two customs declarations and exit permits linked to the case, and participating in the alleged forgery, smuggling and sale of diesel.

Kuwait’s Ministry of Interior previously said that its Criminal Security Sector had uncovered an organised network suspected of illegally exporting petroleum products.

The investigation was carried out by the General Department of Criminal Investigation’s Financial Crimes Department and Sea Ports Investigation Department, in co-operation with the General Administration of Customs.

Authorities began investigating after receiving information about 10 containers prepared for export whose contents allegedly did not match the declared description of the goods as iron.

Investigators subsequently discovered petroleum products inside the containers. The shipments were covered by two customs declarations registered under two commercial companies, according to the authorities.

The case was referred for legal proceedings following an investigation into the suspected smuggling operation and the alleged use of forged customs documents to facilitate the export of subsidized diesel.

The court acquitted the three defendants who had been identified as a customs officer, a Ministry of Interior sergeant and an Egyptian marketing manager, while sentencing the remaining defendants according to its judgment.

title: New review shows ADHD diagnosis links to 71 percent higher mortality risk
author: Kumail Shah
summary: New review shows ADHD diagnosis links to 71 percent higher mortality risk
content:
Adults and children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) have a much higher risk of early death than those without the condition. A new review in JAMA Network Open found that people with ADHD have about a 71% higher risk of dying early, but prescription treatment may help lower this risk.

Researchers reviewed 19 studies that included almost 16 million people from three continents to learn about the long-term health effects of ADHD. They studied both unnatural causes of death, like accidents and suicide, as well as natural causes such as diabetes and heart disease.

The results show that the risk of death is higher in several ways. People with ADHD were 89% more likely to die by suicide. Their risk of dying from injuries, like car accidents, was 55% higher. They also had a 27% higher risk of dying from natural health problems.

Experts say these health risks are linked to factors like higher rates of substance use and smoking. People with ADHD may also have trouble managing chronic illnesses, keeping medical appointments, and following treatment plans because of challenges with executive function.

But the data also showed some hope. Another analysis found that people taking prescribed ADHD medication had a 25% lower risk of dying from any cause compared to those not taking medication. This suggests that proper care can help reduce these risks.

Senior author Joshua Stott, a professor at University College London, said that ADHD is not necessarily life-limiting if people get the right care. However, the authors noted some important points. Since the research was observational, the results show links but not direct cause and effect.

Also, the findings on medication came from only three studies, so these results are still early. Researchers say that while medication helps, people with ADHD need long-term, comprehensive support.

title: Milan back fan boycott of Udinese match over away ticket prices
author: Reuters
summary: Milan back fan boycott of Udinese match over away ticket prices
content:
AC Milan have thrown their support behind supporters planning to boycott Sunday’s Serie A match at Udinese, saying the cost ​of away tickets places an unfair burden on travelling ‌fans.

Tickets for visiting supporters were listed at €65 ($73). In a statement, Milan said excessive pricing risked widening divisions between clubs and undermining efforts to strengthen the ​profile of Italian football.

“The global appeal of Italian football ​depends heavily on the loyalty and passion of supporters of ⁠clubs like AC Milan,” the club said.

“Charging those same fans ​excessive prices for away games is not only unfair, but undermines ​the unity of the league at a time when Italian football needs to come together to compete against the Premier League and other European leagues.”

Milan ​also urged Serie A to consider introducing a league-wide cap on ​away ticket prices, such as England’s Premier League which has a cap of ‌30 ⁠pounds ($40). The club also warned they could adopt a reciprocal policy.

Under the proposal, fans of clubs charging above-average prices to Milan supporters could face higher ticket costs when visiting San Siro, subject ​to league regulations, ​with additional proceeds “donated ⁠to Fondazione Milan to support charitable initiatives”.

“Italian football cannot grow stronger by treating supporters differently based ​on the size of their club,” Milan added.

Ticket pricing ​has ⁠been a longstanding issue for fan group Curva Sud, which boycotted Milan’s away match at Juventus in 2023 in protest.

The supporters’ group renewed ⁠its ​complaints last season over prices charged for ​Milan’s fixtures against Juventus and also accused Torino of overcharging visiting fans.

title: Drinking tea regularly lowers risk of vascular disease by 11 percent, study finds
author: Kumail Shah
summary: Drinking tea regularly lowers risk of vascular disease by 11 percent, study finds
content:
A study published in the Journal of Internal Medicine found that people who drank tea had a lower risk of vascular disease compared to those who did not drink tea.

Researchers followed 485,934 adults in China for about nine years. During that time, 14,863 people developed cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, pulmonary heart, or peripheral artery disease. People who regularly drank tea had an 11% lower risk of these conditions. The lowest risk was seen in those who drank about 6 to 8 cups per week.

Black tea was more consistently linked to a lower risk of vascular disease than green tea. Drinking tea at a moderate strength was tied to the lowest risk. However, drinking tea that was “burning hot” was linked to a higher risk of vascular disease.

“Joint analyses showed that tea consumption, smoking status and physical activity were collectively associated with vascular risk, with the favorable combination of habitual tea consumption, noncurrent smoking and high physical activity associated with the lowest risk,” the authors wrote.

title: Saudi Arabia’s 2025 economic leap: Tourism, manufacturing boom and infrastructure growth
author: Zaeem Basir
summary: Saudi Arabia’s 2025 economic leap: Tourism, manufacturing boom and infrastructure growth
content:
Saudi economy and public services experienced impressive, quantitative economic growth in 2025, fueled by continuous government development projects on the back of Vision 2030.

Figures from the General Authority for Statistics (GASTAT), published in its Services Statistics report, show that four foundational pillars of the Kingdom’s economy – tourism, manufacturing, aviation and health – registered impressive growth.

The tourism and hospitality sector is witnessing unprecedented growth and expansion through a huge hospitality rollout to cater to growing international and domestic travelers.

The number of registered hotels grew by an impressive 31.6%, to reach 2,847 hotels, while total available rooms stood at over 491,000 rooms, marking a year-on-year growth of 23.4%. Serviced apartments increased to 3,090 properties comprising more than 105,000 units and licensed travel and tourism agencies increased by 16.2% to reach 3,177.

Strong growth was also observed in industrial manufacturing, which bolstered national supply chains and manufacturing capacity.

The number of operational factories engaged in manufacturing activity within the Kingdom’s 36 authorized industrial cities grew by 18.9% year on year, to 4,938 facilities, strengthening each city’s contribution to the wider national industrial strategy.

These developments came as the country’s high-capacity air transport network remained stable, with 29 passenger airports providing access to 979,060 domestic and international flights with a total of 140.6 million passenger seats.

Public health, education, civic services tracked for regional populations The public health system registered 292 Ministry of Health hospitals, 63 state-owned others, 2,177 health centers (led regionally by Riyadh, Makkah and Asir) and 515 Saudi Red Crescent emergency ambulance centers; the education system recorded 32,000 schools, fortified by numerous private and public institutions; commercial bank branches increased to 1,910, along with 14,118 automated teller machines.

All these confirmed GASTAT indicators detail data-powered views of a quickly developing economy refining the contours of its many administrative regions and governorates.

title: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released by Russia?
author: Reuters
summary: Who is Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen released by Russia?
content:
President Vladimir Putin announced the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard from Russian detention on Wednesday, at the start of talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

Hubbard, 74, a retired schoolteacher, grew up in Big Rapids, Michigan, and served in ‌the US Air Force and National Guard, according to military records cited by the New York Times.

He earned a master’s degree in English and lived in Japan for 25 years where he taught English before moving to Cyprus and then, in 2014, to Izyum in ​eastern Ukraine with a Ukrainian partner, according to his sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox.

Fox told Reuters in 2024 ​that Hubbard subsisted on a pension of about $300 a month and had few connections with ⁠local people. The siblings last spoke in September 2021.

Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February ​2022 and captured Izyum two months later. Ukrainian forces retook the city in September 2022, but Hubbard was already ​in Russian custody by then.

Russian state media said Hubbard had been detained in April 2022 and alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint. Reuters could not independently establish the circumstances of his capture.

Fox said she recognised her brother in a YouTube video showing ​a man being questioned about his views on Putin and the war. Another video showed him with his hands ​bound, being struck with a sandal. Reuters could not verify when or where the videos were recorded.

Following a ‌closed trial, ⁠a Moscow court convicted Hubbard of being a mercenary in October 2024 and sentenced him to six years and 10 months in prison.Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month. Russian state media said he had pleaded guilty to the charges he faced.

Fox questioned the reported confession, ​however, saying Hubbard held pro-Russian ​views and was unlikely ⁠to have taken up arms in his seventies.

Martin De Luca, his US-based lawyer, told Reuters in June 2025 that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and ​that he was not in any combat or military unit. He cited Hubbard as ​telling him Russian ⁠soldiers had simply grabbed him from his house.

In January 2025, Washington designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained, enabling the US government to pursue negotiations for his release.

The State Department has said Russia refused to grant US officials consular ⁠access.

The ​New York Times reported in February 2025 that Hubbard had been moved ​through at least five Russian detention centres before his trial.

His lawyer said Hubbard’s legal team found out only in April 2025 that he was ​being held in a facility in the Mordovia region, east of Moscow.

title: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
author: Reuters
summary: Government websites go dark after AI-discovered flaw sparks security scramble
content:
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators around the world scrambling to ‌protect their systems.

Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes, opens new tab to vulnerabilities that had quietly been lurking in their software for years until they were uncovered using AI, saying that all users were “encouraged to update immediately.”

With tech firms warning that some hackers were already exploiting the flaws, government agencies across Europe were among those that took sites offline as a precaution.

Because a fix is now public and artificial intelligence tools are able to reverse engineer the bug with little effort, experts said they were bracing for a wave ​of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of fixes.

AI was powering a “race to exploit,” said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity research and incident response firm TLP:Black. He said the next step was the “mass compromise ​of every vulnerable web server on the internet.”

PHP — a language that dates back to the early 1990s and initially stood for “Personal Home Page” — underpins huge parts of the public-facing ⁠web and is baked into WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento sites, meaning that any critical vulnerability potentially has enormous knock-on consequences.

“All servers using any version of PHP released in the last 20 years will be vulnerable,” said Tiffany Farriss, the ​interim chief executive of the Drupal Association. “This issue impacts the majority of the Internet.”

Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied.

The Dutch cybersecurity ​agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. The operator of the online encyclopedia Wikipedia also said it had taken down an unspecified number of systems until they could be safely patched.

Even some world leaders, who don’t typically get involved with software updates, weighed in. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in a post on X said website owners should “check whether your live site uses PHP and prepare to apply the new fix.”

The flaw in PHP was discovered using artificial ​intelligence, Alphabet-owned cybersecurity company Wiz said in a blog post.

The vulnerabilities remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade and would have been extraordinarily complicated for a human hacker to have taken advantage of, the post said.

“Pre-AI, ​this manual work would be difficult to implement and even harder to scale,” it said. “With AI this is no longer a barrier.”

Wiz said its research relied on Wiz Atlas, its autonomous AI vulnerability research tool, as well as Google’s Gemini 4 Argon ‌and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 ⁠Sol. Wiz said it coordinated with the PHP team, OpenAI, and the cybersecurity company Calif on the discovery of the vulnerability and patch verification.

The company said it also partnered with Google Cloud, Cloudflare, Amazon’s AWS, Microsoft, WordPress.com operator Automattic, and other companies such as Fastly, Akamai, Imperva, and Vercel to protect customers and prepare mitigations.

In a statement, the White House said it was made aware of the flaw on Friday.

“This discovery demonstrates exactly why American leadership in SI is so critical,” the White House said, referring to President Donald Trump’s preferred term for artificial intelligence. “This is American innovation strengthening our national security.”

PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP ​assembles the content and sends it to the browser. ​It is free, open-source software maintained by volunteers.

Because of ⁠its ubiquity — PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs — and because the vulnerabilities are considered so dangerous, experts are anxious about a potentially vast pool of sitting ducks. AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have proliferated in recent weeks, would only make things worse, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research ​fellow at King’s College London.

“The scale is huge, and with AI exploitation may happen instantly, on a large scale,” Olejnik said.

The risk is particularly acute for small websites ​run by individuals or organisations ⁠with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly manage the underlying servers. Security experts said such sites could take longer to patch and remain exposed well after fixes become available.

In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites for the country’s five largest political parties and several hospital websites.

Danish municipal IT company ⁠Kombit said it ​had shut down several services, including the national school communication platform.

Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori ​said government public network services had been taken offline “as a precautionary measure.”

France’s Interior Ministry said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance. Japanese cloud service provider Sakura Internet said on Wednesday it had suspended a database appliance function.

title: Mir Raza Ali case: Sindh govt to form new JIT, probe police officers, sources say
author: Asim Mallick
summary: Mir Raza Ali case: Sindh govt to form new JIT, probe police officers, sources say
content:
KARACHI: The Sindh government has decided to form a joint investigation team (JIT) to investigate the Mir Raza murder case on the recommendation of a judicial commission, sources told ARY News.

According to sources, a ministerial committee met Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and presented its recommendations regarding the case.

The JIT will be formed under the supervision of Irfan Baloch, while officials from the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB) and other relevant departments will also be part of the team, sources said.

Sources further said police officers and station house officers (SHOs) nominated in the judicial commission’s recommendations will also face inquiries.

The Sindh government will also prepare a plan for police investigation reforms in light of the judicial commission’s recommendations, sources added.

Earlier, the judicial commission investigating the death of Mir Raza Ali raised serious questions about the police investigation, the handling of medical and digital evidence, and the initial conclusion that he died by suicide.

The commission recommended a new joint investigation team (JIT) to conduct a comprehensive investigation into all aspects of his death.

The 70-page report, headed by Justice Umar Sial, was submitted to the Sindh chief minister on October 15. The commission held 20 meetings between August 27 and October 7 and recorded statements from 50 witnesses.

According to the report, the police initially declared Mir Raza’s death a suicide on the basis of the preliminary post-mortem report. His family challenged that conclusion, citing marks of violence on his body and other evidence.

The police surgeon identified shortcomings in the initial post-mortem report and recommended another examination. Mir Raza’s body was re-examined on August 8. The final report identified a bullet wound entering from the back as the cause of death.

The commission said it was not appropriate to conclude that the death was a suicide while ignoring contradictions in the medical evidence. It criticised the police for maintaining their initial position despite conflicting medical findings and failing to meet basic investigative requirements.

title: Fitbit study shows how extra daily steps protect long-term brain health
author: Kumail Shah
summary: Fitbit study shows how extra daily steps protect long-term brain health
content:
Adding a few more steps to your daily routine can really help keep your brain healthy as you age. A 14-year study in Scientific Reports found that people who walked more each day did much better on tests for focus and self-control. Even 1,000 extra steps a day made a noticeable difference.

Keeping our minds sharp is becoming a big public health issue. In the U.S., cases of mild cognitive impairment are expected to rise from 14.37 million in 2025 to 21.55 million by 2060. Dementia cases could almost double too, going from 7.16 million to 13.85 million.

Earlier studies linked exercise to better brain health and high blood pressure to mental decline, but there was a problem: most studies just asked people how much they exercised, and people often misjudge their own habits.

To get real data instead of guesses, researchers tracked 3,093 adults aged 18 to 93 in the national All of Us Research Program. From 2009 to 2023, participants wore Fitbits to count their daily steps, and doctors recorded their systolic and diastolic blood pressure from medical records.

After 14 years, everyone took four computer tests that measured focus, ability to ignore distractions, planning skills, and how well they could read emotions on faces.

Researchers sorted the participants into three groups based on their activity levels. The least active group walked about 5,100 steps a day. The middle group averaged 8,900 steps, and the most active walked around 14,200 steps daily. Both the middle and most active groups did much better than the least active group when it came to self-control and focus.

Surprisingly, blood pressure had little effect on the mental test scores. The lower blood pressure numbers did not change any of the four test results, and higher top numbers only lowered scores on one decision-making test.

Lower blood pressure explained just 4.8% of the connection between walking and self-control. This suggests that exercise helps the brain in other ways, such as reducing inflammation or helping brain cells use blood sugar.

title: Israel’s election may change its leader, but not Iran war policy
author: Reuters
summary: Israel’s election may change its leader, but not Iran war policy
content:
Israel’s election next week may change its leader, but not its strategy: Iran will remain its chief adversary, military force will continue to be its preferred tool and Palestinian statehood ​a distant prospect, regional policymakers and analysts say.

That is because the strategic assumptions underpinning Israeli policy were hardened by the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israeli communities by ‌Palestinian militant group Hamas and by the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

If anything, Israel could toughen its security policy, the analysts said, as victory for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with the backing of far-right coalition partners could embolden him to step up the war with Iran, tighten Israel’s grip on the occupied West Bank and push diplomacy further to the margins.Israel’s security doctrine now rests on three pillars: breaking Iran, holding buffer zones beyond its borders and using force to deter enemies.

The real ​divide is one of degree rather than direction — how aggressively Israel fights its wars, how far it expands Jewish settlements in the West Bank and whether any leader opts for diplomacy, the ​analysts said.

From Tehran to Riyadh, Tuesday’s election is not seen as a potential turning point but as a test of whether the Middle East is settling into ⁠a long confrontation, where wars ebb and flow while the underlying conflicts are unresolved.

“If Netanyahu is elected, he’ll do whatever he thinks he wants to do,” said Aviv Bushinsky, a former adviser to Netanyahu. “Expansion of ​the settlements will continue. The wars against Iran, Hamas and Hezbollah will continue.””What you see now is what you’ll see after the election, maybe even more aggressively,” he said. “As long as Iran is in such ​a situation, it’s a waste of time talking about Palestine.”

Netanyahu said on Sunday that Israel must prioritise “prevention and offence over containment and defence”, including pre-emptive strikes to thwart emerging threats, while establishing Israel as a regional power and maximising its independence in armaments.

WHY THE COURSE IS UNLIKELY TO CHANGE

The election pits Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud and its ultranationalist allies against an opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party.Palestinian analyst Ghassan al-Khatib sees no prospect of a fundamental shift in ​policy towards the Palestinians, with Israeli political parties competing to project harder-line positions as public opinion moves further to the right.“The substance of the policy remains the same: No to a Palestinian state and ​yes to further settlement expansion. On this, they are all in agreement,” he said.

A government led by Netanyahu’s opponents might seek to repair Israel’s international standing by curbing some settler violence or pursuing settlement expansion with less fanfare. But ‌such changes ⁠would be a shift in style rather than substance, al-Khatib said.

Michael Young of the Carnegie Middle East Center said Israel’s security establishment and much of its political class share a common strategic outlook, centred on confronting Iran, maintaining “forward defence” and preserving military deterrence, reducing the scope for big policy shifts.Joost Hiltermann of the International Crisis Group, who has conducted research in the West Bank, said growing settler violence, mounting Palestinian frustration and the absence of a “political horizon” had created combustible conditions, where even a minor trigger could spark a wider uprising.

Some regional policymakers ask whether Israel’s confrontation with Iran has become the organising principle of Middle East ​security, regardless of who wins the election.

US President Donald ​Trump’s praise of Netanyahu as a “great warrior prime ⁠minister” has reinforced expectations that the Israeli leader will try to finish the campaign against Tehran if he retains power.

Netanyahu has made clear his ambitions extend beyond containing Iran to toppling its clerical rulers.

“Completing the task means toppling the terrorist regime in Iran, the head of the venomous octopus,” he said in a ​speech this week.

But military and political analysts question whether anything short of a US-Israeli ground invasion would force Tehran to abandon what it views ​as its core security interests in ⁠what it sees as an existential fight.After surviving months of war, Iran may be betting it can outlast its opponents while continuing to exert pressure through regional allies.”This is a quagmire,” Young said. “The Iranians can outlast Trump.”Hezbollah in Lebanon and Hamas in Gaza have been weakened, but the broader network of Iran-aligned groups has survived and the conflict could strengthen Tehran’s determination to pursue a nuclear deterrent, the analysts said.For all the alarm Netanyahu ⁠causes in the ​Arab world, some Gulf leaders still see him as the Israeli politician most likely to keep Iran under pressure.

This creates a ​dilemma for them. They oppose what they view as his expansionist policies but want Iranian influence curbed.

“Netanyahu’s policies in Gaza, the West Bank, Syria and Lebanon are damaging,” said Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Gulf Research Center. “As for Iran, a settlement is needed ​before the conflict escalates further. If Iran’s role is not curbed, the region could be heading toward 50 years of Iranian hegemony.”

title: Imam-ul-Haq hits double ton on third day of President’s Trophy Grade-I
author: Web Desk
summary: Imam-ul-Haq hits double ton on third day of President’s Trophy Grade-I
content:
Imam-ul-Haq scored an unbeaten double century for Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against Ghani Glass on the third day of the seventh round of the President’s Trophy Grade-I on Wednesday.

At the LCCA Ground in Lahore, Imam resumed his innings from his overnight score of 118 not out and went on to score an unbeaten 200 as OGDCL declared their first innings at 410 for nine in 102 overs, securing a 178-run lead. Left-handed batter innings included 19 fours and two sixes.

For Ghani, right-arm fast bowler Ubaid Shah took five wickets for 131 runs.

In turn, Ghani who had scored 232 in their first innings, reached 82 for three in 26.3 overs in their second innings, with Hashim Ibrahim and Sharjeel Khan scoring 34 each. They still trail by 96 runs.

At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi, Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) were dismissed for 234 in their second innings after resuming from their overnight score of 111 for two. Mohammad Faiq, who resumed his batting at the overnight score of unbeaten 64, managed to add only two runs before getting out on 66.

Shehzad Gul grabbed five wickets for 61 runs, while Shahnawaz Dahani took three for 66.

Chasing 191 to win the match, Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) finished the day at 87 for four, requiring another 104 runs for win. Test wicketkeeper-batter Mohammad Rizwan returned undefeated on 22.

At the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, Pakistan Television (PTV), following on after being dismissed for 64 in their first innings against MIT Solutions’ 412, recovered to post 394 all out in their second innings.

Waqar Hussain, who resumed on 102 not out, scored 171, while Taimur Khan converted his overnight unbeaten 63 into 151.

For MIT Solutions, Khalid Usman took four wickets for 90 runs as they were set a target of 47 runs.

At the National Ground in Islamabad, State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) posted 398 all out after resuming their first innings at 209 for four against Kingsmen Academy.

Ali Shan remained unbeaten on 100, while Kamran Ghulam contributed 88. Umer Khan took five wickets for 111 runs.

Kingsmen Academy, who had scored 371 in their first innings, reached 166 for two in 28 overs in their second innings, with Mohammad Tayyab Arif scoring 91 and Mohammad Huraira contributing 57.

title: Lost your CNIC? NADRA issues important clarification on FIR
author: Web Desk
summary: Lost your CNIC? NADRA issues important clarification on FIR
content:
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) in Pakistan has clarified that filing a First Information Report (FIR) with the police is not mandatory for citizens seeking a replacement for a lost Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC).

The clarification came in response to a question raised by a citizen on social media, amid what NADRA described as a common misunderstanding about the requirements for replacing a lost identity card.

According to NADRA, it had no policy requiring applicants to submit a copy of an FIR before their application for a replacement CNIC could be accepted or processed.

The authority explained that reporting the loss to the police could be a precautionary measure to help protect citizens against the potential misuse of a lost identity card.

However, it said this was not a compulsory requirement for obtaining a replacement.

Citizens who have lost their CNIC can visit a NADRA registration centre to apply for a replacement or submit their applications through the Pak ID online service, the authority said.

NADRA added that applicants would not be required to provide an FIR copy simply to explain why they were applying for another identity card.

title: ‘We’re paying for his poor planning’: Gandapur’s alleged audio targets Salman Akram Raja
author: Abdul Qadir
summary: ‘We’re paying for his poor planning’: Gandapur’s alleged audio targets Salman Akram Raja
content:
The recording features Gandapur expressing anger over Raja’s recent tweet and accusing him of failing to deliver results despite being given responsibilities.

In the leaked audio, Gandapur says the party is now facing the consequences of Raja’s poor planning, adding that Raja was neither given full authority nor able to deliver.

Gandapur also demanded that Raja immediately delete his tweet, explain his allegations and apologise.

He further claimed that Raja had repeatedly been invited to meetings of the parliamentary committee but had failed to attend.

“We respect him only because of PTI founder Imran Khan,” Gandapur said in the alleged recording, adding that he did not understand who was feeding Raja incorrect information.

The alleged audio has brought internal differences within PTI’s leadership into the spotlight.

Meanwhile, Salman Akram Raja raised concerns about the party’s internal consensus and the situation surrounding the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government.

In his tweet and statement, Raja said undemocratic decision-makers were attempting to undermine consensus within PTI.

He said a narrative was being created that 68 lawmakers were about to announce a new chief minister and had cut off contact with incumbent Chief Minister Sohail Afridi.

Raja urged party workers in Peshawar and other areas not to believe any conspiracy-related narrative until the investigation was complete.

He maintained that Sohail Afridi remained the chief minister under the law and Constitution.

Raja also clarified that Junaid Akbar had been appointed party president in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by PTI founder Imran Khan himself. In Akbar’s absence, Ali Asghar is performing duties as acting president.

The alleged audio and the subsequent statements have brought differences over party strategy, leadership and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government into public view.

title: Laiba Ijaz’s father thanks PM, Mohsin Naqvi, says ‘state is indeed like a mother’
author: Asim Mallick
summary: Laiba Ijaz’s father thanks PM, Mohsin Naqvi, says ‘state is indeed like a mother’
content:
Mohsin Naqvi expressed his sympathies to the bereaved family and offered Fateha and prayers for the forgiveness of the deceased. He also briefed the family on progress in the Laiba Ijaz case.

The interior minister said the entire team had worked day and night on the case and that fulfilling the promise made to the family was a responsibility.

Laiba’s father thanked the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. He said he had heard that the state was like a mother, but the family had now come to believe it.

Islamabad Chief Commissioner, Inspector General of Police and other relevant officials were also present during the visit.

Noman, the main accused in the fraud case involving International Islamic University Islamabad gold medallist Laiba Ijaz, was killed after unidentified men opened fire while police were taking him for a recovery operation.

According to police officials, the incident took place within the limits of Ramna Police Station. The police team was taking the accused, who was in custody, to recover evidence when four unidentified men riding two motorcycles allegedly opened fire in an attempt to free him.

Noman sustained injuries and later died. Police officials said the team remained safe due to bulletproof jackets and other security measures.

A search operation is under way to arrest the accused’s alleged accomplices, police said.

Noman was the main accused in the case involving Laiba Ijaz, who died by suicide after allegedly being defrauded. He had allegedly taken Rs9 million on the pretext of arranging student visas to send students to the United States.

According to police sources, the accused had allegedly carried out similar frauds against dozens of women. He was also accused of sexually harassing 26 women.

Police said Noman admitted after his arrest that he had deceived Laiba and defrauded her.

Laiba had contacted him in February this year through her friend Aiza. The two friends had started an online TikShop business, but it did not succeed.

Aiza’s brother, Azhar, lives in the United States. Laiba had discussed obtaining a US visa through Aiza.

According to the investigation, Noman contacted Laiba from another phone number while pretending to be Aiza. He also created a fake Gmail account in the name of Aiza’s brother, Azhar.

The accused allegedly remained in contact with Laiba through these two fake accounts.

Police said Noman used artificial intelligence to prepare fake documents for Laiba’s student visa.

Investigators obtained part of the chat exchanged between Laiba and the accused. Noman’s mobile phone was sent to a forensic laboratory to uncover further evidence and establish more facts about the case.

title: Waseem Abbas case: Bureau rejects orphanage registration amid ongoing investigation
author: Yasir Sheikh
summary: Waseem Abbas case: Bureau rejects orphanage registration amid ongoing investigation
content:
MULTAN: The Punjab Child Protection and Welfare Bureau has rejected the registration application of Idara Khudi, where 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas was residing before he was deliberately run over by a car in Multan, ARY News reported.

The bureau issued a notification following a meeting of the registration committee held on October 20, 2026.

According to the notification, the committee expressed concerns over the arrangements for the protection and supervision of children at the institution.

The notification stated that the relevant authorities are investigating the facts and circumstances surrounding Waseem Abbas’s death.

The registration committee rejected the institution’s application in light of the recommendations made during its October 20 meeting.

However, the bureau clarified that the rejection of the registration application does not constitute a final determination of criminal responsibility or establish fault on the part of any individual.

The Punjab Child Protection and Welfare Bureau has also issued a letter to the general secretary of Idara Khudi.

Meanwhile, police have registered cases under child labour laws against Touqeer Nazir, the main accused in Waseem Abbas’s death, and Shoaib, the owner of the orphanage where the teenager had been living.

According to police, the cases were registered on the complaint of the Labour Department over alleged violations of child labour laws.

An FIR against Touqeer Nazir was registered at DHA Police Station, while a separate case against orphanage owner Shoaib was registered at BZU Police Station.

Police said Waseem had been living at the orphanage before being handed over to Nazir to learn electrical work. The teenager was subjected to forced labour while working under the contractor.

The orphanage owner, Shoaib, was already in police custody in connection with the investigation, sources said.

Meanwhile, Touqeer Nazir was killed in an alleged encounter with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur on Wednesday, police said.

CCD officials said police attempted to stop two motorcyclists near the Northern Bypass in Bahawalpur. However, the suspects allegedly opened fire while trying to flee.

title: Pakistan overtake Australia in ICC ODI Rankings
author: Web Desk
summary: Pakistan overtake Australia in ICC ODI Rankings
content:
DUBAI: Pakistan have superseded Australia in the latest International Cricket Council (ICC) ODI rankings, announced on Wednesday.

The Green Shirts moved to fourth place with 103 rating points, replacing Australia after securing consecutive victories over Sri Lanka and England in the opening two matches of the ODI tri-series.

Meanwhile, South Africa retained the third place, having 104 points. India continued to remain at the top position with 115 points closely followed by New Zealand with a difference six rating points.

Pakistan opened their tri-series campaign with a 37-run victory over Sri Lanka. Salman Ali Agha starred with a century, propelling the home side to a big total of 305.

In reply, Sri Lanka were bowled out for 268 in 48.1 overs, chiefly due to impressive bowling from Pakistan fast bowlers. Shaheen Afridi led the bowling charts with a three wicket haul.

In the second fixture against England, Pakistan showcased a dominant all-round display, posting 302-9 in 50 overs after lower-order heroics. Hasan Nawaz top-scored with 79 while Arafat Minhas also made a valuable contribution with 59.

The pair rescued Pakistan from a difficult situation, adding a 78-run partnership for the sixth-wicket, which took the total over 200-run mark.

In pursuit of the target, the visitors were bowled out for 215 in 38.4 overs. Minhas tore through their middle-order and picked up a career-best six wicket haul.

Minhas took 6 for 40 in 8.4 overs and earned the player of match award for his all-round display.

title: US Democratic congressional nominee Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank
author: Reuters
summary: US Democratic congressional nominee Lander detained by Israeli authorities in West Bank
content:
TEL AVIV: Brad Lander, an ‌ally of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani who is running ​for the US Congress ​next month, was among 90 ⁠individuals detained by Israeli ​authorities in the occupied West ​Bank on Wednesday while accompanying Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, according to Rabbis ​for Human rights, an ​Israeli rights group.

Lander is a Jewish ‌American ⁠and former New York City comptroller and mayoral candidate who has criticized Israel’s war ​in Gaza. ​He ⁠is the Democratic party’s nominee for New ​York’s 10th congressional district ​for ⁠the US House of Representatives.

Read Also:Israeli settlers burn olive trees, injure journalist in West Bank attack

Earlier, Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 people in the West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government.

Police said they raided several locations across the occupied territory and seized cars and potential evidence related to the attacks.

The arrests come as violence increases in the West Bank, with Israeli settlers disrupting the annual olive harvest of Palestinians.

“Following the severe incidents of violence over the past weekend, including the assault of a media worker and the suspected attacks on foreign civilians, an arrest operation was conducted before dawn,” said Major General Moshe Finchi, the Israeli police’s West Bank commander.

“Suspects were arrested on suspicion of involvement in the violent incidents, violating a military commander’s order concerning a closed military zone, and illegal construction,” he said.

title: Authors urge UK to halt ‘draconian’ Palestine Action ban as Rooney sales end
author: AFP
summary: Authors urge UK to halt ‘draconian’ Palestine Action ban as Rooney sales end
content:
London,: More than 150 writers and personalities signed an open letter Wednesday urging the UK government to amend its “draconian” ban on Palestine Action after Irish author Sally Rooney said she was halting book sales in Britain as a result.

The Labour government has been heavily criticised by some for proscribing Palestine Action as a “terrorist” group in July 2025, with thousands of people arrested since for protesting against the move.

“Sally Rooney is a writer, not a terrorist. Her books must be available to the public,” said the letter signed by such notable figures as Nobel laureates Annie Ernaux and Anne Carson.

Rooney and her publisher Faber last week announced they had to end the sale of her books in the UK because of her support for the pro-Palestinian group.

The proscription, which the organisation is appealing, puts Palestine Action on the same blacklist as militant groups Hamas and Hezbollah, making it illegal in the UK to be part of, support or finance it.

Rooney has repeatedly expressed her support for Palestine Action and said she intends to fund the group, which is not proscribed by Ireland, where the author lives and works.

Faber said the ban meant it could not legally pass on royalties earned in the UK to Rooney, whose best-sellers including “Normal People” and “Intermezzo” have earned her praise as the “voice of a generation”.

Read Also:West Bank on verge of ‘explosion’: senior Palestinian official

“Their withdrawal from sale, on the basis of ill-conceived and draconian anti-terror legislation, is an affront to basic principles of free speech and expression so long taken for granted in this country,” the open letter, also signed by actors Paul Mescal and Tilda Swinton, adds.

“We categorically reject censorship – whether direct or indirect – and urge the government to change course, amending the legislation which has led us to this point of repressive absurdity.”

Other signatories include authors Colm Toibin, Arundhati Roy, Jhumpa Lahiri, Zadie Smith and Julian Barnes.

Last week, police said they were looking into a social media post by Sarah Helm, the wife of the UK’s national security advisor, for supporting the group — although they later said it did not merit a criminal investigation.

Palestine Action’s stated goal on its website is to end “global participation in Israel’s genocidal and apartheid regime”.

Its proscription came after a series of high-profile stunts protesting the war in Gaza, including targeting weapons factories, especially those belonging to Israeli arms group Elbit.

Britain’s Supreme Court is set to hear an appeal against the ban from the group’s cofounder Huda Ammori next month.

title: JI announces third phase of Islamabad long march against petroleum levy from Oct 23
author: Web Desk
summary: JI announces third phase of Islamabad long march against petroleum levy from Oct 23
content:
LAHORE: Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) Pakistan on Wednesday announced the third phase of its long march towards Islamabad from October 23 to press the government to abolish the petroleum levy and provide relief to the public.

JI Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch said the third phase of the Islamabad long march would begin on October 23, with protest demonstrations to be held at all district headquarters across the country on the same day.

Baloch described JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman’s call for nationwide protests as a timely move, reiterating that the party would continue its struggle for the withdrawal of the petroleum levy and relief for the people.

He said the government had proposed that the negotiating committees of both sides meet before a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hafiz Naeemur Rehman.

Baloch urged the two negotiating committees to finalise their recommendations at the earliest, saying JI had so far received no information about any progress by the government’s negotiating team.

He maintained that the party would not back down from its principled and constitutional position on public issues.

JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman had announced a long march towards Islamabad on September 20 to protest against the petroleum levy. However, the party later postponed the march following a telephone call from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Addressing a press conference in Multan, Hafiz Naeem said the march had been temporarily postponed at the prime minister’s request, following his assurance that he would meet the JI leadership after returning home to find a solution to the issue.

However, the proposed meeting has yet to take place.

Earlier, addressing party workers in Lahore, Hafiz Naeem said JI had not deviated from its existing strategy.

Read Also:JI Amir says PM meeting expected within two days on levy issue

He said no political party had raised its voice over the petroleum levy when JI began highlighting the issue, adding that the public had been largely unaware of the levy a few months earlier.

Hafiz Naeem maintained that the levy was unrelated to the actual price of petrol and described it as a “jaga tax”.

The JI chief said the party had blocked roads, staged sit-ins, organised rallies and strikes, and launched a long march, adding that it had not abandoned its protest movement.

title: Jansen takes five for South Africa as Australia forced to follow on
author: AFP
summary: Jansen takes five for South Africa as Australia forced to follow on
content:
Marco Jansen took five wickets as Australia crashed to 99 all out in reply to South Africa’s first innings of 425-9 declared on the fourth day of the second Test at St George’s Park on Wednesday.

With a first innings lead of 326 runs, South Africa enforced the follow-on despite fast bowler Anrich Nortje being out of action with a groin injury.

Tall left-armer Jansen struck with his first ball of the innings when he had nightwatchman Scott Boland caught behind in the second over of the day.

He followed up with the wickets of Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Alex Carey and Beau Webster as Australia collapsed.

Steve Smith, who twice needed treatment for what appeared to be a neck injury, top-scored for Australia with 28 before being bowled by Wiaan Mulder.

Australia 99 (K. Rabada 2-33, M. Jansen 5-33, W. Mulder 2-14).

Match situation: South Africa lead by 326 runs on the first innings and have enforced the follow-on.

title: Rodri needed a rest for Barcelona ahead of Clasico, says Flick
author: AFP
summary: Rodri needed a rest for Barcelona ahead of Clasico, says Flick
content:
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said Rodri would be back in the starting line-up for Sunday’s Clasico showdown against Real Madrid after being rested at kick-off in the Champions League loss away to Paris Saint-Germain.

“Yes, but you know Rodri played a lot of minutes with the national team and also the last games with us,” Flick told reporters after Barcelona’s 4-2 defeat in Paris on Tuesday.

“I spoke with him this morning and I told him that we made this decision, and Marc Bernal started instead. For me, it was a good solution what we did and hopefully he is fresh on Sunday.”

Rodri came on after an hour of the game in Paris, as Barcelona’s perfect record this season came to an end.

The Catalans had twice come from behind, with Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal replying to goals by Desire Doue and Lucas Hernandez for the hosts.

Yamal made it 2-2 in the 79th minute, but Vitinha put PSG back in front two minutes later before Fabian Ruiz sealed the victory for the defending European champions.

“I think it was a fantastic game from both teams but we made too many mistakes, especially in possession,” Flick said.

“But I also saw a lot of good things. For me it was a great test for us and you also saw today what errors we have to improve to make things better.

“We have to learn from this game. Today, in October, you cannot win titles. You win the Champions League in June.”

Flick added that the upcoming Clasico, in which Barca have the chance to go nine points ahead of Madrid in La Liga, influenced his team selection “a lot”.

Barcelona lost Dani Olmo to injury in the French capital, while the home team saw Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, two of their chief attacking stars, come off hurt.

Dembele suffered a hamstring injury in the first half, and captain Marquinhos was also unable to finish the encounter.

“I am not the doctor but the three players are injured which is the worst thing to come out of tonight’s game,” said PSG coach Luis Enrique.

“Three injuries to three very important players. It is the worst news we could have had, but that is what happens in football.”

PSG have won their first three games in this season’s league phase, scoring 14 goals in the process, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third year running.

They are therefore comfortably on course to reach the knockout phase, although their coach is not getting carried away. The top eight teams in the league phase go straight through to the last 16.

“We have already played against our two opponents from Pot A,” he said, with this win following a 4-2 triumph at Manchester City last week.

“But I will remind you that last year we also won our first three games and we did not finish in the top eight.

“We will enjoy this but then we will start to think about this weekend’s game against Lyon.”

title: US aims to loan about a third of heating oil reserve in bid to tame prices
author: Reuters
summary: US aims to loan about a third of heating oil reserve in bid to tame prices
content:
WASHINGTON: The Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the 1-million-barrel ‌US emergency heating oil reserve, the Department of Energy said on Wednesday, in a bid to tame prices, which have surged on diesel shortages due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.

The move, reported first by Reuters, came after senators from both political ​parties urged the administration to release heating oil from the reserve as prices for diesel, a fuel from ​the same refining stream, hit records above $6.50 per gallon on disruptions across the Middle ⁠East caused by the Iran war.

The administration will evaluate whether further releases from the reserve are necessary, a ​source at the department said.

The US has only tapped the Northeast Home Heating Oil Reserve once since Hurricane Sandy ​struck the region in 2012. The emergency stockpile is held at sites in New Jersey, Connecticut, Massachusetts and Maine.

About one-third of New England homes use heating oil and about half in Maine.

Soaring heating oil costs have emerged as a key issue ahead of the November 3 elections, including ​in several tight Senate races, as Trump’s fellow Republicans are trying to maintain control of the two chambers of ​Congress.

Maine Republican Senator Susan Collins is facing a tough reelection fight, while New Hampshire’s open Senate seat is a toss-up between ‌Democrat ⁠Chris Pappas and Republican John Sununu. In Alaska, Republican Senator Dan Sullivan is facing a challenge from Democrat Mary Peltola.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the administration was “committed to doing everything in our power to lower energy costs.” The department said there would be a competitive bidding process for the loans for both fuel retailers and terminal holders ​to allow the fuel to ​flow into areas facing ⁠shortages.

The administration is also backing the Williams Companies’ (WMB.N), opens new tab Constitution natural gas pipeline project, which would ship natural gas produced in Pennsylvania to heat homes in New York and New England.

​This week, the US released up to $42 million in Cold War-era Defense Production Act funding ​for initial ⁠work on Constitution. New York has blocked the project on environmental grounds.

The department will loan up to 315,000 barrels of heating oil from Maine, Massachusetts and Connecticut, it said. Deliveries are set to be completed by November 13.

The Trump administration ⁠is ​also struggling to control crude oil prices that have risen from ​the Iran war and has already agreed to loan 172 million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Levels in that emergency stockpile, held ​on the coasts of Texas and Louisiana, are at their lowest since 1982.

title: Gold prices decline in Pakistan amid losses in global bullion markets
author: Anjum Wahab
summary: Gold prices decline in Pakistan amid losses in global bullion markets
content:
KARACHI: Gold prices extended their downward trend in Pakistan on Wednesday, tracking losses in international bullion markets as rising oil prices fuelled inflation concerns and reinforced expectations of tighter US monetary policy.

The price of 24-karat gold per tola fell by Rs900 to Rs434,536, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association.

Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold declined by Rs772 to Rs372,544, while 10 grams of 22-karat gold fell by Rs707 to Rs341,511.

In the international market, gold prices dropped by $9 to $4,120 per ounce, the association reported.

Silver prices also declined locally, with the price per tola falling by Rs27 to Rs6,207. The price of 10 grams of 24-karat silver decreased by Rs23 to Rs5,321.

International silver prices fell by $0.27 to $57.29 per ounce, according to the association.

Rising energy costs have heightened concerns about persistent inflation, potentially limiting the US Federal Reserve’s ability to ease monetary policy.

“Gold has adhered to the downtrend that began 2 months ago,” said Han Tan, chief market analyst at Bybit.

Investors are also awaiting the US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data due next week. The Federal Reserve closely monitors the index as its preferred measure of inflation against its 2% target.

Stronger-than-expected consumer and producer inflation data released last week indicated that US price pressures remained elevated amid surging energy costs.

Oil prices rose by more than $1, with Brent crude futures holding above $110 a barrel as escalating tensions in the Middle East fuelled fears of supply disruptions.

Gold is traditionally regarded as a hedge against inflation and a safe-haven asset during periods of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. A weaker US dollar can also make the metal more affordable for buyers using other currencies, potentially supporting demand.

Read More:Oil rises on Middle East supply fears, US inventory drawdowns

However, traditional safe-haven assets have delivered mixed performance amid market volatility this year. Concerns over the Iran war, elevated energy prices, uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence-linked technology stocks and mounting government debt have added to investor uncertainty.

title: Mehmoodabad Police Encounter: Suspect behind K-electric meter reader shooting nabbed
author: Afzal Khan
summary: Mehmoodabad Police Encounter: Suspect behind K-electric meter reader shooting nabbed
content:
KARACHI: Mehmoodabad police, following an encounter, arrested an injured suspect involved in yesterday’s shooting of a K-Electric meter reader, ARY News reported.

The police encounter occurred near TP2, resulting in the arrest of the wounded suspect.

Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East stated that the suspect, identified as Rabi Raffaiel, had opened fire on the K-Electric meter reader while the worker was performing his duties.

The SSP further informed that arms and ammunition were recovered from the suspect’s possession, while a search for his accomplices remains underway.

According to the SSP, the suspect has a prior criminal record and has previously been jailed for theft, robbery, and illegal possession of arms.

Earlier, a K-Electric meter reader was critically injured in a targeted firing incident in the Mahmoodabad area of Karachi on Tuesday.

Unidentified assailants opened fire on the meter reader, who sustained five to six gunshot wounds.

Meanwhile, another meter reader accompanying him managed to escape unharmed by fleeing the scene.

Following the attack, the perpetrators fled the spot on a motorcycle.

The injured employee was rushed to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) for emergency treatment.

Meanwhile, police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) regarding the incident and initiated an investigation.

The K-Electric spokesperson responding on the incident said that an extremely unfortunate incident of firing at K-Electric staff who were on duty was reported in Mehmoodabad. One injured employee is being provided medical assistance, says K-Electric spokesperson.

K-Electric management is in constant contact with the injured employee’s family and is extending all possible support, says K-Electric spokesperson.

The incident has been reported to law enforcement agencies. K-Electric is extending its full cooperation in investigating the incident and establishing the motive behind it, says K-Electric spokesperson.

K-Electric considers the safety of its field staff a top priority and strongly condemns the attack on its personnel while on duty. Strict legal action will be pursued against those involved, says K-Electric spokesperson.
