title: Pakistan, Maldives sign 20 MoUs to strengthen bilateral ties
author: Hamid Ur Rehman
summary: Pakistan, Maldives sign 20 MoUs to strengthen bilateral ties
content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and the Maldives on Wednesday signed 20 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) to strengthen bilateral cooperation across multiple sectors, including defence, information technology, cybersecurity, health, education, social protection, agriculture and tourism.

The agreements were signed during the three-day state visit of Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, the first visit by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years. The visit coincides with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Muizzu witnessed the signing ceremony, during which representatives of the two sides exchanged the documents.

The agreements cover cooperation in information technology, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, digital skills, technology and innovation. The two countries also signed an MoU to strengthen collaboration in combating the illicit trafficking and abuse of narcotic drugs.

Other agreements focused on social protection, health cooperation and collaboration between the Maldives Food and Drug Authority and Pakistan’s Drug Regulatory Authority. The two sides also signed MoUs on the recruitment of health professionals, defence cooperation and maritime security.

To expand agricultural ties, the countries signed an MoU on agricultural cooperation, along with another agreement to promote cooperation in fisheries.

Read Also:Pakistan, United States discuss advancing bilateral trade agreement

In the education sector, the two sides agreed to collaborate on technical and vocational education and training, as well as broader educational cooperation.

The representatives also exchanged documents on MoUs covering youth and sports development, air connectivity, tourism, and cooperation in arts, culture and heritage.

Additional agreements were signed between the Maldives Police Service’s National College of Policy and Law Enforcement and Pakistan’s National Police Academy in Islamabad; the Maldives Civil Service Commission and Pakistan’s Federal Public Service Commission; and the Maldives Civil Service Commission and Pakistan’s Civil Service Academy.

To promote commercial engagement, an MoU was signed between the Maldives State Trading Organisation (STO) and the Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) to facilitate trade in agricultural commodities, food and other products.

The two countries also signed an agreement to strengthen cooperation in environmental protection, further broadening the scope of their bilateral partnership.

title: PHC hears petitions about missing provincial minister, MNA
author: Usman Danish
summary: PHC hears petitions about missing provincial minister, MNA
content:
PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Wednesday heard petitions with regard to disappearance of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) provincial minister Fazal Shakoor Khan and Fazal Muhammad MNA, ARY News reported.

The high court bench comprises of Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Fahim Wali heard the case.

Investigation Officer informed the court on question that geo-fencing has been conducted, and efforts are ongoing for recovery of the disappeared persons.

The court observed that an FIR has been registered in the case of Faza Muhammad MNA.

Petitioner’s lawyer Bashir Khan Wazir told the court about providing USB to police.

Assistant advocate general Mohammad Adnan Sher said that the petitioner is not providing USB to police.

Petitioner’s lawyer said that the USB has been given to Chamkani police, while the minister’s brother has also recorded his statement.

The lawyer said that the investigation officer of the provincial minister’s case not coming to the court.

“This is the state of affairs in the country, provincial minister and the MNA are going missing with no trace,” Justice Ijaz Anwar observed. “Where the prominent persons have been missing, what will be the condition of the general public,” Justice Anwar questioned.

The lawyer told the bench that other cases of similar nature, have been fixed on November 03, pleading the court to club these cases with them.

The PHC bench adjourned further hearing of the recovery petitions until November 03.

title: Putin says US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed: Russian media
author: AFP
summary: Putin says US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed: Russian media
content:
SAINT PETERSBURG, Russia: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced Wednesday the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American taken captive by Russian forces years ago in Ukraine, during a meeting with US special envoy Steve Witkoff, news agencies reported.

Putin had said that Hubbard was at Pulkovo Airport in Saint Petersburg, Russian news agencies reported, adding that Witkoff, who was meeting with the Russian president in the city, had thanked Putin for the release.

Hubbard, a retired English teacher in his 70s, was sentenced in a closed trial in October 2024 to nearly seven years in prison for “mercenary work” on behalf of Ukraine, a charge he denies.

Wednesday’s announcement came as US President Donald Trump’s special envoy met to brief Putin on his meeting with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo a day earlier, which Witkoff described as “productive”.

Trump had said on Tuesday that he had asked Putin for Hubbard’s release.

“I’ve been talking to him at length. I’ve asked him to release him. Let’s see what happens,” Trump told journalists in Washington.

On Wednesday, Witkoff said Trump and “our whole nation sends their thanks because of Stephen Hubbard,” calling Putin a “humanitarian”.

title: Minor maid allegedly beaten to death by employers in Sheikhupura
author: Web Desk, Muhammad Irfan
summary: Minor maid allegedly beaten to death by employers in Sheikhupura
content:
SHEIKHUPURA: Influential individuals allegedly tortured a 12-year-old maid to death in Sheikhupura, ARY News reported.

The tragic incident occurred at a house located on Khalid Road in Sheikhupura. The minor, identified as Zainab, had been working as a domestic helper at the residence of Chaudhry Rafaqat for the past year and a half.

Family members of the deceased child accused the homeowner’s wife of subjecting the young girl to brutal beatings with sticks, which ultimately caused her death.

Police transferred the body to a nearby hospital for medico-legal procedures.

Meanwhile, law enforcement officers arrested one suspect in connection with the torture and are conducting raids to apprehend the remaining individuals involved.

Earlier, a 15-year-old boy, Waseem Abbas, was killed after being hit by a speeding car in a private housing society in Multan. Police have arrested the contractor accused of chasing the teenager in a vehicle.

According to police, the main suspect, Touqeer Nazir, has been arrested, the vehicle taken into custody and a case registered. Further investigation into the incident is underway.

In his initial statement to police, Touqeer Nazir said Waseem had been learning electrical work from him. He claimed the boy would leave work without permission and that he had tried to catch him.

The suspect said he drove the car behind Waseem because he wanted to stop him, according to his initial statement.

Police earlier said the boy had left the job and was chased by the contractor. The suspect allegedly pursued him on foot before following him in a car along with another man, Amjad Ali.

During the chase, the speeding car struck Waseem. He hit the gate of a house and died at the scene, police said.

According to orphanage administrator Jawad Haider, Waseem Abbas was an orphan who lived at an orphanage.

Haider said Waseem had been handed over to Touqeer Nazir to learn electrical work.

The deceased was a resident of Muzaffargarh and was 15 years old.

Police said further investigation into the circumstances surrounding Waseem’s death was ongoing.

title: Anthropic logged net loss of over $80 billion in first half of 2026
author: Reuters
summary: Anthropic logged net loss of over $80 billion in first half of 2026
content:
Anthropic’s net loss widened sharply to $80.7 billion in the first half of this year, in large part due ​to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into shares of the ‌AI startup, according to a draft prospectus for a planned initial public offering that was reviewed by Reuters.

The San Francisco-based company is expected to go public in November and some investors are now weighing a lower valuation of around $1.5 trillion ​following its latest financial disclosures, Reuters reported last week.

Its first-half loss, widening from a loss of $13 ​billion a year earlier, included a $72 billion accounting charge reflecting an increase in the ⁠estimated value of bonds that could eventually convert into Anthropic shares, rather than cash costs tied to ​its operations, the document said.

The disclosures underscore the hefty costs of the AI race even as investors ​give greater scrutiny to whether the vast sums being poured into chips and data centers will generate sufficient returns.

Anthropic has committed to spending at least $518 billion over a decade on cloud services, computing and infrastructure.

The company spent nearly $9 billion on ​computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half, up from $2.3 billion a year earlier, the S-1 document ​showed.Anthropic did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

At an investor meeting on October 14, Anthropic told ‌prospective IPO ⁠investors that its third-quarter revenue jumped 45% to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

While the figures eased some concerns about the enormous costs of developing AI systems, some investors were disappointed by the slowing sequential growth rate. Revenue had more than doubled from the first ​quarter to $11.6 billion in ​the second quarter.

A cooler ⁠reception for Anthropic’s IPO could weigh on the wider AI market, whose near-term prospects investors see as hinging largely on the share sale’s success, ahead of ​rival OpenAI’s potential listing next year.

Elon Musk gave his clearest signal yet that he’s seriously considering combining his rocket company SpaceX with his car company Tesla,

Reuters reported in September that Anthropic posted a ​net loss ⁠of $42 billion in 2025, with most of that stemming from a similar accounting charge. As Anthropic’s valuation climbed, the estimated fair value of those notes tripled year over year.

Excluding the charge, Anthropic posted an operating loss of ⁠about $8.1 ​billion on $4.6 billion of revenue in 2025.The company has benefited from ​the popularity of Claude Code, its coding assistant that developers use to write software and build apps.

title: UGREEN unveils new charging line-up in the UAE and Saudi Arabia following iPhone 18 launch
author: Muhammad Abuzar Usama
summary: UGREEN unveils new charging line-up in the UAE and Saudi Arabia following iPhone 18 launch
content:
UGREEN has introduced new MagFlow and Nexode charging products in the UAE and Saudi Arabia, offering more charging options for users of the new iPhone 18 line-up and other Apple devices.

The new releases include magnetic wireless charging stands, power banks and wired chargers, with products designed for use with iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, iPad, and MacBook.

The expanded line-up caters to a variety of charging needs, from powering multiple devices at a desk to keeping phones charged on the go. With new desktop and portable charging options, UGREEN aims to give Apple users greater flexibility in how and where they charge their devices.

The UGREEN MagFlow Pro 3-in-1 Magnetic Wireless Charging Stand 25W brings iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods charging together on one stand. It supports up to 25W Qi2 wireless charging for compatible phones and uses thermoelectric active cooling to help manage heat during charging.

A built-in display shows charging power and temperature, while the adjustable stand allows users to position their phone for viewing. Together, these features combine multi-device charging and detailed monitoring in a single desktop set-up.

For portable charging, the MagFlow Air Magnetic Power Bank is available in 25W and 15W versions, each with a 10,000mAh capacity. Strong built-in magnets allow the power banks to attach securely to compatible devices for wireless charging on the go.

The 25W version also includes a built-in USB-C cable supporting up to 45W wired charging, while the power bank itself supports up to 30W input for recharging. This gives users the flexibility to choose between wired and wireless charging without carrying an extra cable.

The Nexode Air 65W Charger provides a wired option for compatible USB-C phones, tablets and laptops. It uses GaN technology in a compact design with a foldable plug, making it suitable for use at a desk or when travelling.

It delivers up to 65W of power, depending on the connected device, and features temperature monitoring and built-in electrical safety protections.

The line-up also includes the Nexode Pro Mini Power Bank 45W, a compact 10,000mAh power bank that offers up to 45W wired charging. Its palm-sized design makes it easy to carry, providing another portable charging option alongside the magnetic MagFlow Air models.

This new charging line-up is now available through Amazon and noon in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

title: Pakistan pushes sovereign cloud, AI-Powered trade ecosystem for commerce ministry
author: Web Desk
summary: Pakistan pushes sovereign cloud, AI-Powered trade ecosystem for commerce ministry
content:
ISLAMABAD: Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan held separate meetings with representatives of the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) and the management of Sky47 to explore the development of a secure, integrated and AI-enabled digital ecosystem for the Ministry of Commerce and its attached organizations.

The meetings focused on treating government data as a national asset, strengthening Pakistan’s sovereign cloud and data-centre infrastructure, enabling secure data exchange, and utilizing artificial intelligence for evidence-based trade and export policymaking, said a press release issued here on Friday.

Commerce Minister pushes sovereign cloud, AI-Powered trade ecosystem for Pakistan

Jam Kamal Khan said the Ministry of Commerce maintains extensive information relating to thousands of tariff and product lines, exporters, international markets, trade bodies, chambers of commerce, business associations and overseas trade missions.

He stressed that this dispersed information must be standardized, integrated and made readily available to authorized users in secure and decision-friendly formats.

“Pakistan’s trade data is a valuable national asset. It must be protected, properly classified and transformed into actionable intelligence for exporters, businesses and policymakers,” the Minister said.

He emphasized the need to connect the Ministry’s wings, attached departments, the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan, chambers and trade associations, as well as Pakistan’s trade officers serving in more than 55 countries.

He also called for greater integration of the Ministry’s digital portals to provide a unified view of trade-related activities and market intelligence.

The Pakistan Digital Authority briefed the Minister on the emerging national framework for data governance, data exchange, enterprise architecture and cloud adoption. The meeting discussed the classification of government data into categories such as open, shared, restricted and personally identifiable information, while preserving the ownership and control of data with the respective ministries and public bodies.

It was emphasized that government departments should share only the information required for a particular purpose instead of transferring complete datasets. The proposed data-exchange mechanism would facilitate secure, standardized and traceable interdepartmental access while preventing misuse of confidential and personal information.

The participants also discussed the establishment of a national digital master plan, under which sector-specific digitalization roadmaps could be developed in coordination with federal and provincial governments, public institutions and the private sector.

Jam Kamal Khan highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence to analyze trade trends, identify export opportunities and assist in preparing market-specific policy recommendations. He said an indigenous AI platform trained on authorized government and sectoral datasets could become a powerful tool for economic planning and public service delivery.

The meeting with Sky47 focused on Pakistan’s data-centre capacity, sovereign cloud services, cybersecurity, disaster recovery and the growing computing requirements associated with artificial intelligence.

The Sky47 team briefed the Minister on its data-centre infrastructure and plans to expand secure and reliable hosting capacity in Pakistan.

The Minister was informed that modern data centres could provide highly reliable services aligned with international standards while reducing the cost and security risks associated with numerous small and fragmented departmental facilities.

The discussions also covered energy-efficient cooling systems, intelligent data storage, metadata management, data-fabric technologies and the separate computing requirements of conventional applications, AI models and future quantum-computing workloads.

The Minister stressed that Pakistan must build sufficient local capacity to host critical national data within the country, ensuring data sovereignty while enabling innovation and investment in cloud computing, artificial intelligence and digital services.

The meetings further examined reforms in public-sector technology procurement. Participants underlined the need for cloud-procurement frameworks that allow government organizations to obtain infrastructure, platforms and software as services without facing unnecessarily lengthy and outdated procedures.

The Minister supported closer coordination among the Pakistan Digital Authority, Ministry of Commerce, PPRA, IPO Pakistan and other stakeholders to develop mechanisms for supporting startups and innovators. Such frameworks could allow successful prototypes developed in response to government challenges to move towards transparent, fast-track procurement and wider deployment.

The potential establishment of an Open Network for Digital Commerce, adapted to Pakistan’s requirements, was also discussed. The proposed network could digitally connect producers, exporters, logistics providers, financial institutions and consumers while opening new opportunities for small and medium enterprises.

Jam Kamal Khan also expressed concern over the use of publicly available foreign AI platforms for confidential official work. He called for clear guidelines, awareness and secure domestic alternatives to prevent sensitive government correspondence and institutional data from being transferred to unauthorized external systems.

He directed the relevant teams to continue technical consultations and develop practical proposals for secure data integration, sovereign cloud adoption, AI-enabled trade intelligence and digital-commerce infrastructure.

The Minister said the Ministry of Commerce would work closely with the Pakistan Digital Authority, Sky47 and other stakeholders to ensure that Pakistan’s digital transformation directly contributes to export growth, better governance, innovation and long-term economic competitiveness.

title: Iran says Saudi Arabia, Houthis have not answered mediation offer
author: Reuters
summary: Iran says Saudi Arabia, Houthis have not answered mediation offer
content:
CAIRO: Iran has not received a response ​from Saudi Arabia or Yemen’s Houthis ‌to its offer to help broker talks to end the fighting between them, Iranian Foreign Minister ​Abbas Araqchi said in a television ​interview aired on Tuesday.

Araqchi offered to ⁠help facilitate dialogue as the Iran-aligned Houthis intensified ​strikes on Saudi Arabia earlier this month.

In ​the interview with Iraq’s Al Ekhbariya TV, Araqchi also responded to the possibility of Egypt joining Saudi ​Arabia in the war against the ​Houthis.

“Any foreign intervention would complicate matters,” he said, adding ‌Cairo ⁠has previously told Tehran that it would “not directly” interfere in the Yemeni conflict.

Egypt has said it is ready to provide ​Saudi Arabia with ​the ⁠support it needs to defend its security, potentially raising the stakes ​in the Middle East.A vote ​in ⁠the Egyptian parliament on a possible move against the Houthi fighters by the country’s ⁠military, ​one of the Arab ​world’s largest, was delayed until October 26.

title: Man sentenced to death for sexually assaulting stepdaughter in Islamabad
author: Web Desk
summary: Man sentenced to death for sexually assaulting stepdaughter in Islamabad
content:
ISLAMABAD: A district and sessions court in Islamabad on Wednesday sentenced a man to death for raping his stepdaughter repeatedly over a period of one year in the absence of her mother.

The court also ordered the convict, identified as Iftikhar, to pay Rs3.5 million in fines and compensation to the victim and the child born as a result of the crime.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Muhammad Sohail announced the verdict after finding the accused guilty.

According to the written judgment, the court sentenced Iftikhar to death and imposed a fine of Rs500,000. It also ordered him to pay Rs1 million in compensation to the victim and Rs2 million for the care and maintenance of the child.

The court relied on forensic evidence presented during the trial. DNA testing conducted by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency linked the accused to the crime.

According to the judgment, the DNA profile of the child born following the assault matched that of the convict, supporting the prosecution’s case.

The case was registered at Shahzad Town Police Station in February 2025 on the complaint of the victim’s mother.

After examining the evidence, the court convicted Iftikhar and handed down the death sentence, along with the fine and compensation orders.

The judgment further directed the convict to bear the financial responsibility for the child’s care and maintenance by paying Rs2 million.

Rawalpindi child sexual assault and murder case: Suspect killed in alleged CCD encounter

title: Kvaratskhelia set for months out with torn ACL
author: AFP
summary: Kvaratskhelia set for months out with torn ACL
content:
Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia requires surgery after tearing his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona, the European champions said on Wednesday.

“Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement.

In more bad news for PSG, the club said forward Ousmane Dembele and central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for “several weeks” with injuries.

Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark in the 4-2 league phase victory against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday.

The 25-year-old Georgia international played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles and is one of the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, which will be awarded on Monday.

Dembele, the current Ballon d’Or holder, and Marquinhos both suffered thigh injuries, PSG said.

title: Pakistani software developer arrested in Lahore over $126 million US Postal Service scam
author: Hamid Ur Rehman
summary: Pakistani software developer arrested in Lahore over $126 million US Postal Service scam
content:
LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has arrested Pakistani software developer Faheem Akram in Lahore over his alleged involvement in a $126 million fraud involving counterfeit US postage labels, officials said.

According to the NCCIA, Faheem Akram allegedly operated a website to sell counterfeit US postage labels, causing estimated losses of more than $126 million to the United States Postal Service (USPS).

NCCIA officials said the suspect had been wanted by US authorities in connection with the alleged fraud, which involved the online sale of more than five million counterfeit postage labels.

Addressing a press conference, NCCIA Lahore Zone Additional Director Atif Ameer said the suspect had operated the website LabelsBank.com from August 2023 to September 2026, marketing and selling counterfeit US postage labels online.

Ameer said the website allegedly bypassed the US Postal Service’s official system by offering counterfeit labels at uniform prices for packages of different types and sizes. The suspect allegedly sold approximately 5.1 million labels to customers in the United States while operating from Pakistan.

According to the official, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) traced the suspect and shared information with Pakistani authorities, leading to the investigation and subsequent arrest.

The NCCIA spokesperson said investigators had uncovered the use of 16 bank accounts belonging to the suspect’s family to transfer money allegedly obtained through the scheme.

Laiba’s uncle reveals how family lost millions in US scholarship scam

A 10-day operation was conducted to locate and arrest Akram. During the operation, investigators questioned 47 people and analysed 122 call records, the spokesperson said.

Eight special teams, working under the supervision of Additional Director Atif Ameer, conducted raids at 35 locations across Punjab, Islamabad and Sindh before arresting the suspect in Lahore.

The agency has registered a case against Akram, while further investigations into the alleged fraud and the movement of funds are under way.

NCCIA Director General Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi reviewed the operation during a video conference with senior officers, including Deputy Director Hassan Sajjad Naqvi, Lahore Deputy Director Waqas Saeed and Additional Director Atif Ameer.

Rizvi congratulated the officers involved in the operation and praised their professionalism, hard work and investigative strategy. He directed officials to continue pursuing cybercriminals and said protecting citizens from financial fraud, online scams and other cybercrimes remained a key responsibility of the agency.

title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League
author: AFP
summary: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League
content:
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.

Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.

PSG kept their place at the top of the league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.

“We don’t feel superior to any team but we trust in ourselves, in everyone who starts and who comes off the bench,” Paris midfielder Ruiz told Movistar. “There’s still a long way to go.”

Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.

“We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today,” said Flick, whose team had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.

Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.

PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.

Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.

Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.

The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header.

Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.

But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.

Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.

Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.

Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner.

Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.

Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.

“We are facing very good teams. It’s good to come back but we’ve started losing too many goals this season,” Iraola told Amazon Prime.

At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, before Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend.

AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios, only for Rayan Cherki to sweep in City’s third in the 57th minute.

Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.

“Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction,” Foden told TNT Sports of his gradual return to form.

Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.

All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.

Massimiliano Allegri’s men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.

Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.

Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.

title: Boiler explosion at Port Qasim factory left one laborer dead another injured seriously
author: Afzal Khan
summary: Boiler explosion at Port Qasim factory left one laborer dead another injured seriously
content:
KARACHI: A boiler exploded at a chemical factory located in Port Qasim, killing one laborer and leaving another severely burned, ARY News reported.

According to police, the explosion resulted in one casualty and left another worker critically injured. Both victims were rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment.

Hospital sources stated that the condition of the injured worker remains critical.

Police further informed that welding work was underway to repair the boiler when the explosion occurred.

Earlier, the Sindh Government decided to pursue zero-tolerance policy against private schools being run in dangerous and dilapidated buildings, ARY News reported on Tuesday.

The education department of the Sindh government has directed for immediately discontinuing educational activities in dangerous buildings. The department has also ordered launching a comprehensive inspection of private school buildings within 15 days.

The managements have been directed to shift schoolchildren to alternative safer places with the warning that presence of children, teachers and other staff in dangerous premises will not be tolerated.

In schools’ survey, the buildings will be examined, and dangerous and partly damaged buildings will be pointed out.

Sindh education department has instructed schools associations to enforce the building safety standards immediately.

The authorities have also decided to review registration of the private schools being run in dilapidated buildings. “Legal action will be taken against the schools in dangerous buildings, which could be closed if required”.

The unregistered educational institutions will be traced, and legal action will be taken against them.

The authorities have summoned report with regard to the schools’ inspection with dangerous premises and affected students within 15 days.

title: Sooryavanshi told to be patient by captain Iyer ahead of NZ series
author: AFP
summary: Sooryavanshi told to be patient by captain Iyer ahead of NZ series
content:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi “can’t just walk straight into the team”, India captain Shreyas Iyer said Wednesday, after calls for the teenage sensation to be unleashed for the T20 series against New Zealand starting in Christchurch this week.

The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made his international debut for India in July but has been used sparingly against top opponents despite his glittering Indian Premier League form.

India landed in New Zealand on Tuesday, two days before they begin their 40-day tour including five T20s, five one-day internationals and two Test matches.

It marks 100 years of sporting ties between the two nations.

“He has many more years ahead to get opportunities,” Iyer said when asked about the teenager’s role in the squad.

“It’s not as if he can just walk straight into the team right now because our openers have been scoring consistently and also won us the World Cup.”

Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm after making his IPL debut aged 14 years and 23 days in 2025.

Nine days later he scored his first IPL century.

In eight T20 internationals Sooryavanshi is averaging just over 30 at a strike rate of 186, below his IPL average of 44 and strike rate of nearly 229.

Since July Sooryavanshi’s rivals for India’s opening spot, Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma, have averaged 25 and 30 respectively, at strike rates of 172 and 200.

Iyer said Sooryavanshi would learn plenty from the tour, with or without game time.

“Look at it this way: coming overseas like this will give him a fair idea of how the game plays on these particular wickets, so next time when he comes he will be very well prepared for these conditions.”

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said he was aware of Sooryavanshi’s talents from playing in the IPL but pointed to the power of India’s whole lineup.

“I think he has a huge part to play for India, whether it’s in this series or in the future,” Santner said.

“If he does get a crack guys have found it quite hard to stop him, but we’ve got some plans for him.”

Santner said conditions would be seam friendly in the opening match at Hagley Oval.

India would have to get used to some unfamiliar conditions as they start the series, he said.

“Temperature-wise, you know, we’ve always when we’ve gone to India, it’s hot, it’s humid,” Santner said.

“Here tomorrow night could be the flip side for India, could be a little bit cold, maybe windy, some cold hands.”

New Zealand are without Will O’Rourke, Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes for the T20 series but will be able to lean on the power hitting of Finn Allen and Tim Seifert at the top of the order.

India recalled seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar after a four-year absence while Jasprit Bumrah was rested as part of workload management after he played a key part in the team’s recent Asian Games gold medal in Japan.

title: Waseem Abbas death: Touqeer Nazir, orphanage owner booked in child labour cases
author: Web Desk
summary: Waseem Abbas death: Touqeer Nazir, orphanage owner booked in child labour cases
content:
MULTAN: Police have registered cases under the child labour law against Touqeer Nazir, the main accused in the death of 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas, and Shoaib, the owner of the orphanage where the child had been living.

According to police, the cases were registered on the complaint of the Labour Department over alleged violations of child labour laws.

An FIR against Touqeer Nazir was registered at DHA Police Station, while a separate case against orphanage owner Shoaib was registered at BZU Police Station.

Police said Waseem had been living at the orphanage before being handed over to Nazir to learn electrical work. The teenager was subjected to forced labour while working under the contractor.

The orphanage owner, Shoaib, was already in police custody in connection with the investigation, sources said.

Meanwhile, Touqeer Nazir was killed in an alleged encounter with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur on Wednesday, police said.

CCD officials said police attempted to stop two motorcyclists near the Northern Bypass in Bahawalpur. However, the suspects allegedly opened fire while trying to flee.

The CCD said one man was killed in the exchange of fire and was later identified as Nazir. Police have not provided further details about the encounter.

Waseem was killed a day earlier after being struck by a speeding car allegedly driven by Nazir in a private housing society in Multan. CCTV footage of the incident also surfaced.

Police had arrested Nazir in connection with the teenager’s death and seized the vehicle involved in the incident. A murder case was registered against him following the incident.

On Tuesday, a court remanded Nazir in police custody for four days for further investigation. However, he was killed before the completion of the remand period.

Waseem Abbas case: Main accused Touqeer Nazir killed in CCD encounter

In his initial statement, Nazir claimed that the teenager would leave work without permission and that he had tried to stop him.

Police said Nazir chased Waseem, initially on foot and later in a car, accompanied by another man identified as Amjad Ali.

During the pursuit, the speeding vehicle struck Waseem, causing him to collide with the gate of a house. The teenager died at the scene, police said.

Nazir had claimed that he was trying to stop Waseem when his car skidded and struck the teenager. He said he had spotted Waseem near a street corner and accelerated to position his vehicle ahead of him to block his way.

According to the suspect’s account, the car failed to stop after skidding, while Waseem slipped and became trapped between the vehicle and the house’s gate.

title: ECP Issues Schedule for Islamabad Local Government Elections
author: Hassan Ayub
summary: ECP Issues Schedule for Islamabad Local Government Elections
content:
ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday formally released the schedule for the local government elections in Islamabad, ARY News reported.

Polling for the local body elections will be held on December 20 in Islamabad, with candidates able to submit their nomination papers from November 2 to November 6.

Election symbols will be allotted to candidates on November 26. Voting will take place without any break from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM on polling day.

Following the issuance of the schedule, the ECP imposed a ban on the transfer and posting of government officials in the federal capital.

Under the ECP guidelines, the Prime Minister, President, ministers, and members of parliament are barred from participating in the election campaign for Islamabad’s local government elections. Additionally, the electoral body has banned the announcement of any new development projects in the capital.

title: Sehat Dehleez اpp launched for free medical consultations with qualified doctors
author: Hamid Ur Rehman
summary: Sehat Dehleez اpp launched for free medical consultations with qualified doctors
content:
QUETTA: The Balochistan government has launched a telehealth application, “Sehat Dehleez,” to provide free medical consultations with qualified doctors to people across the province, particularly those living in remote areas.

Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti announced the initiative in a statement on X, saying the service had received an encouraging response during its first 24 hours of operation.

According to Bugti, the platform received 791 consultation calls on its first day, while 495 consultations were completed. A total of 718 calls included location information, and the service reached people in 35 districts across Balochistan.

He said the initiative was aimed at making healthcare more accessible to people in remote areas who face difficulties reaching medical facilities, particularly during extreme weather conditions.

“The overwhelming response to Sehat Dehleez across Balochistan is a clear reflection of the trust and confidence of our people,” Bugti said, adding that the government was working towards building a healthier and stronger province.

The chief minister said the application offered free consultations with qualified doctors around the clock, covering general health, maternal and child health, and guidance on common illnesses.

Balochistan police announces fresh job opportunities

The initiative has been introduced by the People’s Primary Healthcare Initiative (PPHI) Balochistan to improve access to timely medical advice through digital technology.

According to PPHI Balochistan, the platform enables residents to consult doctors from their homes, reducing the need for travel, particularly for people living in areas where access to healthcare facilities is limited.

The service also aims to provide health awareness and guidance on common illnesses, with a focus on maternal and child healthcare.

PPHI Balochistan said the telehealth initiative was designed to make healthcare services more accessible, convenient and responsive to public needs through digital technology.

Residents can access the Sehat Dehleez service through its web application and Android app by scanning the QR codes provided by the organisation.

The initiative marks an effort to expand digital healthcare services across Balochistan and improve access to medical consultation for residents throughout the province.

title: Musk ordered reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine: report
author: AFP
summary: Musk ordered reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine: report
content:
WASHINGTON: Elon Musk ordered a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday, after the tech billionaire said any limits on the SpaceX-operated communications system would ultimately have come from the president.

Musk capped the speed at which Ukrainian equipment could connect to the system, making some of Kyiv’s drones useless, the Journal reported, citing anonymous US officials and people familiar with the matter.

Kyiv has accused Washington of deliberately slowing speeds at which Starshield can be used effectively — a charge denied last week by US President Donald Trump.

Musk had previously said that “any limits on speed or usage” of Starshield systems were “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” referring to Trump.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Wednesday that Washington had no prior knowledge of the slowdown.

“The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr. Musk,” Rubio said during his trip to India.

“That’s a private company; the president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything… I’m telling you, there was no foreknowledge.”

On Tuesday, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said that the Pentagon had not directed any changes to Starshield, saying: “We haven’t pulled anything back.”

“Nothing’s changed from our view. We haven’t made any directives or anything like that,” he said.

Trump said last week he did not request any curbs to Starshield, adding: “It wasn’t me. And I don’t think it was Elon.”

Kyiv last week reported restrictions to the service, which it sees as crucial to fending off Moscow’s invasion, shortly after Trump criticized Ukraine and urged it to stop targeting Russian oil refineries.

Ukraine uses Starshield, Starlink’s military-grade satellite service, for its battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russia-occupied territory, and its interceptor drones. It also uses SpaceX’s parallel Starlink civilian satellite system.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have been increasingly tense in recent days, with Trump calling for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to be replaced after he criticized a US deal allowing more Russian diesel into global markets.

title: National savings increases profit rates across multiple schemes
author: Shoaib Nizami
summary: National savings increases profit rates across multiple schemes
content:
ISLAMABAD: The profit rates on National Savings Schemes have been increased by 36 to 110 basis points, ARY News reported.

The profit rate on Special Savings Certificates jumped to 12 percent following an uptick of 110 basis points. Similarly, the rate on Regular Income Certificates climbed to 12.12 percent after an increase of 96 basis points.

Additionally, the profit rate on Behbood Savings Certificates reached 12.96 percent after a 36-basis-point raise. Furthermore, the rate on the Sarwa Islamic Savings Account increased by 59 basis points to 11.84 percent.

title: Husband arrested for killing wife weeks after love marriage in Karachi
author: Afzal Khan
summary: Husband arrested for killing wife weeks after love marriage in Karachi
content:
KARACHI: A 21-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her husband just one and a half months after their love marriage in New Karachi, police said on Wednesday.

The victim, identified as Sawera, was found dead at her husband’s house. Her family has accused her husband, Sarfaraz, of being involved in her murder.

According to the victim’s mother, Zeenat, Sarfaraz was already married before marrying Sawera, making the marriage his second.

Zeenat alleged that other people were also involved in her daughter’s murder and called for a thorough investigation into the case.

She appealed to Sindh Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho to ensure protection for her family and bring those responsible to justice.

She also expressed concerns over the investigation, alleging that the police were not investigating the case properly.

Zeenat said Sawera was an orphan whom she had raised despite facing severe financial and personal difficulties. She demanded justice for her daughter and punishment for those responsible for her death.

Police said the investigation was ongoing and further action would be taken after the DNA report was received.

Karachi Defence woman death case: Husband gives statement, family declines legal action

Earlier, the body of a 36-year-old woman was found in a residential flat in Defence Phase 8 on Monday, ARY News reported, citing police.

The deceased was identified as Shumaila. According to the initial police investigation, she was suspected of having died by suicide after severing her hamstrings.

Police shifted the body to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) for an autopsy and completion of the necessary legal formalities.

Police said Shumaila’s husband told investigators that his wife had injected a boil on her wrist. Her family also informed police that her mental health was not stable.

South SSP Mahzoor Ali said the deceased woman’s brother had refused to pursue legal action in the case.

Following the discovery of the body, police had launched an investigation to gather further information about the woman, her family and the circumstances surrounding her death.

title: Oil rises on Middle East supply fears, US inventory drawdowns
author: Reuters
summary: Oil rises on Middle East supply fears, US inventory drawdowns
content:
BEIJING: Oil prices gained over $1 on Wednesday as escalating Middle East tensions fuelled fears of supply disruptions, while falling US crude and product inventories lent support to the market.

Brent crude futures rose $1.61, or 1.5%, to $110.40 per barrel as of 0630 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) ​crude gained $1.45, or 1.5%, to $99.27 per barrel.

Prices fell in the previous trading session after Iran’s president discussed mediation efforts in ​a meeting with Pakistan’s army chief in Tehran, though Brent hit a five-month ⁠high before easing.

“Oil prices have been having a bit of wild ride in the last couple of ​sessions,” said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS.

“We believe this is a mix of profit taking ​and optimistic hopes of a Qatar- or Pakistan-brokered deal, countered by the realisation that any deal is still very distant and compounded further by inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), which shows drawdowns continuing in the US for both crude ​and products.”

Iran told Pakistan’s army chief there would be no talks with Washington until its demands were met, ​Iranian media outlet Nournews reported on Tuesday, adding that a Qatari delegation had arrived in Tehran. There was no official confirmation ‌of the ⁠reports.

Maritime security risks are also escalating. Shiptracker Kpler said on Monday that at least 18 vessel attacks were recorded over the past two weeks, while LSEG analysts warned Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and the ship-to-ship transfers ​supporting regional loadings.

In Saudi Arabia, the ​Houthis on Monday claimed ⁠responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh and Abha airports.

The death toll from a Houthi attack on ​Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas ​Araqchi said in ⁠a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen’s Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.

Wall Street stocks finished mostly higher Tuesday with the Dow adding about one percent,

In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they were ⁠working ​with refiners around the world to boost fuel output as a diesel ​shortage has raised prices.

According to market sources citing API data, US crude stocks fell by 4.9 million barrels in the week ended October ​16.

title: FCCP reinstates three ATC judges removed by Sindh govt
author: Hussain Ahmed Chaudhry
summary: FCCP reinstates three ATC judges removed by Sindh govt
content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court of Pakistan (FCCP) on Wednesday reinstated three Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) judges who were removed by the Sindh government following amendments to the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, imposing an upper age limit of 65 years for judges of such courts.

The court set aside the order of a division bench of the Sindh High Court’s Circuit Court at Hyderabad and declared the provincial government’s notification removing the judges to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

The case was brought by Muhammad Yameen, Ubaidullah Khan and Syed Zakir Hussain, who challenged the application of amendments introduced through the Anti-Terrorism (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2025, to judges appointed for fixed terms before the amendments came into force.

Under the amended Section 14 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, judges and presiding officers of Anti-Terrorism Courts are required to relinquish office upon attaining the age of 65. The amendment was published in the official Gazette on September 2, 2025.

The Sindh government subsequently issued a notification directing the three judges to cease holding office with immediate effect, although their stipulated terms had not expired.

The judges challenged the notification before the Sindh High Court, seeking permission to continue serving until the completion of their respective tenures. However, the high court dismissed their petitions, ruling that the amended age limit applied to judges already holding office as well as future appointees.

The petitioners then approached the FCCP. The counsel, Salahuddin Ahmed, argued that the amended provisions could not be applied to appointments made before the legislation came into force.

Opposing the petition, Additional Advocate General Sindh Barrister Sandeep Malani and Additional Prosecutor General Sindh Siraj Ali Khan Chandio maintained that the amended provisions also applied to judges already in office.

The FCCP examined whether the newly introduced age limit could curtail the fixed tenures of judges appointed under the previous law.

In its ruling, the court held that the amending legislation contained neither an express provision nor any necessary implication extending the new age limit to existing fixed-term appointments in a manner that would shorten their tenure.

The court observed that judges appointed for a specified period under the law then in force had acquired a vested right to hold office for that period, subject to the applicable conditions governing the continuation or premature termination of their appointments.

Read More: Bushra Bibi’s sentence suspension appeal dismissed by FCCP

It further held that where an amended provision admits of two reasonably possible interpretations, the interpretation preserving the existing right should be preferred.

Accordingly, the court ruled that the newly prescribed age limit could not be applied to existing fixed-term appointments to curtail their remaining tenure.

Setting aside the Sindh High Court’s order, the FCCP declared the provincial government’s notification unlawful and without legal effect.

The court further ruled that the petitioner, Muhammad Yameen, would be deemed to have remained in office despite the notification and would be entitled to continue as Judge/Presiding Officer of Anti-Terrorism Court-IV, Karachi, until the completion of his stipulated two-and-a-half-year term, subject to the conditions governing his appointment under the law.

title: Guardian consent given before child was placed with contractor, says center head
author: Yasir Sheikh
summary: Guardian consent given before child was placed with contractor, says center head
content:
MULTAN: The guardian of Waseem Abbas, the child who met a tragic death at the hands of contractor Tauqeer Nazir, was taken into confidence before the boy was handed over to the contractor, ARY News reported.

Speaking to ARY News, Shoaib Hyder, head of the orphan center Khudi, stated that Waseem’s paternal uncle was his legal guardian. According to Hyder, the uncle requested that the child be trained to earn a living. Under this request, Waseem was placed with Tauqeer to learn electrician work.
