He added that the center is currently registered with the Punjab Charity Commission.

The center presently cares for 150 orphans. The late Waseem Abbas was admitted to the institution in 2021 along with his brother and cousin.

Earlier, a 15-year-old boy, Waseem Abbas, was killed after being hit by a speeding car in a private housing society in Multan. Police have arrested the contractor accused of chasing the teenager in a vehicle.

According to police, the main suspect, Touqeer Nazir, has been arrested, the vehicle taken into custody and a case registered. Further investigation into the incident is underway.

In his initial statement to police, Touqeer Nazir said Waseem had been learning electrical work from him. He claimed the boy would leave work without permission and that he had tried to catch him.

The suspect said he drove the car behind Waseem because he wanted to stop him, according to his initial statement.

Police earlier said the boy had left the job and was chased by the contractor. The suspect allegedly pursued him on foot before following him in a car along with another man, Amjad Ali.

During the chase, the speeding car struck Waseem. He hit the gate of a house and died at the scene, police said.

According to orphanage administrator Jawad Haider, Waseem Abbas was an orphan who lived at an orphanage.

Haider said Waseem had been handed over to Touqeer Nazir to learn electrical work.

The deceased was a resident of Muzaffargarh and was 15 years old.

Police said further investigation into the circumstances surrounding Waseem’s death was ongoing.

title: World falling ‘dangerously short’ on climate action: UN chief
author: AFP
summary: World falling ‘dangerously short’ on climate action: UN chief
content:
PARIS: Global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions are falling far short of the Paris climate goals and put the world on course for 2.6C warming this century, the UN warned Wednesday.

The report by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) lays bare the chasm between rhetoric and action when it comes to tackling global warming, and the challenge before political leaders at November’s COP31 climate summit.

Even if countries deliver their latest climate pledges in full, global temperatures could still rise 2.6C above pre-industrial levels by 2100, said the annual Emissions Gap Report.

That would blow past the historic goal agreed in Paris: keeping warming well below 2C while striving for a safer 1.5C. Any chance of keeping to 1.5C had been “lost” due to decades of insufficient climate action, the report said.

“The world can no longer avoid overshooting the 1.5 degree limit, and the consequences are already devastating,” said UN chief Antonio Guterres in a statement to launch the closely-watched report.

“Deadly floods, brutal heatwaves, raging wildfires, lost lives, crippled economies, deepening inequalities, and those least responsible are suffering first and worst.”

Overall, global greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 were broadly on a par with record levels in 2024, with the difference between the two years too small to call, the report said.

Carbon emissions just from burning coal, oil and gas — the main driver of climate change — rose slightly in 2025 compared to the previous year.

Guterres said deep and immediate cuts were needed to protect humanity from worsening impacts but instead “emissions remain at record levels. And national climate plans and current policies fall dangerously short”.

Sticking just with current policies would see warming hit 2.8C, the report said.

Scientists warn that every additional fraction of a degree above 1.5C increases extreme weather events and the likelihood of irreversible changes to the planet, from dying coral reefs to melting permafrost.

The world has already warmed roughly 1.4C relative to pre-industrial times and crossing 1.5C is expected in a matter of years.

The G20 accounts for three-quarters of global emissions but Guterres said “all countries, especially the big emitters, must do more” to stop heating the planet.

This latest UNEP warming outlook is worse than last year’s due to the formal withdrawal of the United States from the Paris accord and upward revisions of historical emissions, said report co-author Anne Olhoff.

Emissions growth slowed down among the G20 but the US was a “major exception”, it added.

Among the world’s top-six emitters, preliminary data for 2025 showed emissions increases in the US, Indonesia and China and decreases in India, Russia and the European Union.

But in terms of magnitude, the US increase of 133 megatons of CO2 equivalent “far exceeded” that of any other country, driven by higher electricity demand and a rebound of coal power generation.

The next-largest increase was recorded in Turkey, which is hosting the UN climate summit in Antalya from November 9-20.

The US is the world’s second-largest polluter, behind China. US President Donald Trump has called climate change a hoax and rolled back clean energy policies while boosting fossil fuel production.

UNEP executive secretary Inger Andersen told reporters that no country was shielded from climate change and impacts were being felt “on every nation on the planet, including the US”.

The report details a scenario with a 50 percent chance of bringing global warming back down to 1.5C by 2100.

To get there, warming must peak around 1.8C by 2050 and vast amounts of carbon dioxide would have to be removed from the atmosphere to bring temperatures down further.

But this scenario assumes immediate emissions cuts of six percent per year, every year, until 2035 — nowhere near current projections.

“The main takeaway is simple — governments need to get on with enacting policies that cut fossil fuel use as soon as possible,” said Bill Hare, CEO of global policy institute Climate Analytics.

Some climate-vulnerable developing nations have accused bigger emitters of abandoning the Paris goals and a showdown over the 1.5C target is expected at COP31.

“This is a historic failure of political leadership. The science has been clear for decades, but governments have chosen delay over action. The consequences will be measured in lives lost, not just degrees of warming,” said Mohamed Adow, director of Kenya-based think tank Power Shift Africa.

Guterres agreed there was a climate “leadership gap” but said overshooting 1.5C “is not surrender”.

title: Nine die, 39 injured in Rajanpur bus accident
author: Web Desk
summary: Nine die, 39 injured in Rajanpur bus accident
content:
RAJANPUR: At least nine persons were killed, and 39 others were injured in a road accident at Indus Highway in Rajanpur district, rescue officials said on Wednesday.

A bus carrying passengers from Karachi to Dera Ghazi Khan met a deadly mishap when collided with road divider in Rojhan leaving eight people dead on the spot, officials said.

The deceased included women and children, rescue agencies said. The dead bodies and the injured were shifted to Rajanpur District Hospital.

The death toll increased to nine as a passenger succumbed to his injuries at the hospital.

“Among 39 injured, 13 have been in a precarious condition,” according to officials.

Five persons were killed in a road accident in Multan on Monday when a speedy car hit the road divider.

The road mishap took place in the historic city of Multan when a speedy car crashed with the road divider at Bosan Road causing fire in the vehicle’s engine, officials said.

“The firefighters extinguished the fire in the car, retrieved five dead bodies from the vehicles and shifted them to the Nishtar Hospital of the city,” rescuers said.

Three persons died in the accident have been identified as Muzammil 23, Yasir 22 and Ramazan 28 years of age.

The identities of two other deceased, also in their 20s, with 25 and 24 years of age, have yet to be established, rescue officials said.

The deceased belong to Shuja Abad tehsil of Multan district.

title: Multan: Waseem Abbas’s postmortem report reveals severe head injuries
author: Hamid Ur Rehman
summary: Multan: Waseem Abbas’s postmortem report reveals severe head injuries
content:
MULTAN: The initial postmortem report of 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas, who was run over by a car in Multan, was released on Wednesday, revealing severe head injuries and multiple fractures.

According to the report, Waseem sustained a severe head injury that damaged his brain, which led to his death.

The report also identified a fracture in his spinal bone, along with bruises and abrasions on his arms and other parts of his body.

It further stated that the left side of the teenager’s head and face was severely affected. Fractures were also found in his upper jaw and nasal bones, while an abrasion was observed on his right knee.

Read More: Waseem Abbas case: Touqeer Nazir killed in CCD encounter

Touqeer Nazir, the main accused in Waseem’s death, was killed in an alleged encounter with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD) on Wednesday, police said.

According to the CCD, Nazir had escaped from police custody in Multan, prompting police to launch efforts to apprehend him.

CCD officials said they attempted to stop two motorcyclists near the Northern Bypass in Bahawalpur. However, the suspects allegedly opened fire while attempting to flee.

The CCD said one man was killed in the exchange of fire and was later identified as Nazir. Police have not provided further details about the encounter.

Earlier, Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Bokhari described Waseem’s death as a tragic incident that had shaken the public. In a statement posted on X, she said women and children were Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s “red line” and that such crimes would not be tolerated in Punjab.

According to Bokhari, Waseem belonged to Muzaffargarh. His father died when he was very young, and his mother later married a man named Jafar. Waseem had three siblings, and all the children had been placed in an orphanage.

The minister said Waseem’s sister had left the orphanage six months earlier to live with their mother, while one of his brothers remained at the institution.

She added that Waseem had been handed over to a contractor, Touqeer Nazir, about a week before the incident to learn electrical work.

On October 19, Waseem reportedly fled after being mistreated at his workplace. According to the minister, Nazir and his accomplice, Amjad, chased him in a car for approximately one kilometre before running him over.

title: Toddler dies, brother critical after consuming contaminated dairy milk
author: Ahmer Khokhar
summary: Toddler dies, brother critical after consuming contaminated dairy milk
content:
LAHORE: A two-year-old child allegedly died after drinking contaminated milk purchased from a local dairy shop in the Nishtar Colony area of Lahore. Meanwhile, his three-year-old brother, Zain, is in critical condition after consuming the poisonous milk, ARY News reported.

According to details, a family in Lahore bought milk from a neighborhood dairy shop. Shortly after feeding it to the children, the younger child, Faizan, passed away, while his brother fell seriously ill.

Both children were rushed to Lahore General Hospital for medical treatment, where one was pronounced dead and the other remains in critical condition.

The Superintendent of Police (SP) Model Town stated that the parents had purchased the milk from a local dairy vendor, leading to the tragic incident. Police have arrested two individuals associated with the dairy shop.

Additionally, forensic experts and the Punjab Food Department were called to collect milk samples for analysis.

The forensic team and food department staff have collected the samples and will release a report determining the exact cause of the child’s death.

title: NADRA clarifies B-form procedure for children without mother’s CNIC
author: Hamid Ur Rehman
summary: NADRA clarifies B-form procedure for children without mother’s CNIC
content:
ISLAMABAD: The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has clarified the procedure for obtaining a child’s B-Form, also known as the Child Registration Certificate (CRC), when the mother’s Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) is unavailable.

In a statement shared through a NADRA podcast, Public Information Officer Syed Shabahat Ali explained that the procedure depends on whether the mother’s CNIC has been issued but is currently unavailable or has never been issued.

If the mother’s CNIC has already been issued but she does not have the card at the time of NADRA centre visit, the absence of the physical document may not pose a major problem. According to NADRA, her identity can be verified through her CNIC number or biometric verification, including fingerprints.

However, if the mother has never been issued a CNIC, obtaining the child’s B-Form may become more difficult because the relevant family records and supporting documents must be complete to obtain the B-Form.

NADRA officials explained that in such cases, the parents’ marriage may not have been registered in the official record, and a family number may not have been issued. These gaps in the family record can create difficulties in processing the child’s registration.

Parents facing this situation may need to resolve the missing identity or family registration records before proceeding with the child’s B-Form application.

Separately, NADRA has outlined the procedure for obtaining a replacement B-Form if a child’s existing document has been lost.

Read More: NADRA explains how to replace a lost B-Form

Applicants can visit their nearest NADRA Registration Centre or apply from home through the Pak ID mobile application.

According to NADRA, the replacement fee is Rs50 under the normal category and Rs500 under the executive category.

The B-Form, officially known as the Child Registration Certificate, is an important document used to register children in Pakistan’s national database.

title: Waseem Abbas case: Main accused Touqeer Nazir killed in CCD encounter
author: Web Desk
summary: Waseem Abbas case: Main accused Touqeer Nazir killed in CCD encounter
content:
MULTAN: Touqeer Nazir, the main accused in the death of 15-year-old orphan Waseem Abbas, was killed in an alleged encounter with Punjab’s Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur on Wednesday, police said.

According to the CCD, Nazir had escaped from police custody in Multan, prompting police to set up a roadblock to apprehend him.

CCD officials said they attempted to stop two motorcyclists near the Northern Bypass in Bahawalpur. However, the suspects allegedly opened fire while trying to flee.

The CCD said a man was killed in the exchange of fire and was later identified as Touqeer Nazir.

Police have not provided further details about the encounter.

Waseem was killed a day earlier after being struck by a speeding car driven by Touqeer Nazir in a private housing society in Multan. CCTV footage of the incident also surfaced.

Police had arrested Nazir in connection with the teenager’s death and seized the vehicle involved in the incident. A murder case was registered against him on a police complaint.

On Tuesday, a court remanded Nazir in police custody for four days for further investigation. However, he was killed before the completion of the remand period.

According to police, Waseem had been learning electrical work under Nazir. In his initial statement, the suspect claimed that the teenager would leave work without permission and that he had tried to stop him.

Police said Nazir chased Waseem, initially on foot and later in a car, accompanied by another man identified as Amjad Ali.

During the pursuit, the speeding vehicle struck Waseem, causing him to collide with the gate of a house. The teenager died at the scene, police said.

Waseem Abbas case: Contractor claims car skidded, child slipped into its path in Multan

Nazir had claimed that he was trying to stop Waseem when his car skidded and struck the teenager. He said he had spotted Waseem near a street corner and accelerated to position his vehicle ahead of him and block his way.

According to the suspect’s account, the car failed to stop after skidding, while Waseem slipped and became trapped between the vehicle and the house’s gate.

title: US envoy to meet Russia’s president after ‘productive’ talks with Zelensky
author: AFP
summary: US envoy to meet Russia’s president after ‘productive’ talks with Zelensky
content:
SAINT PETERSBURG, Russia: US envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Saint Petersburg and meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday following “very productive” talks with Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky.

The trip by Donald Trump’s special envoy is part of efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between Kyiv’s leader and the US president over the war with Russia.

After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence on Russian strikes.

The positive tone followed days of friction between Kyiv and Washington after Trump struck a diesel-supply deal with Putin and called for Zelensky to be replaced after Ukraine refused to stop hitting Russian oil refineries.

“We are thankful that intelligence works,” Zelensky told reporters in Oslo, describing the early warnings as “very, very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians” when ballistic missiles were about to strike.

Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, whose country hosted Tuesday’s talks, said Witkoff would next travel to the Russian city of Saint Petersburg.

Witkoff’s meeting with Putin on Wednesday would include Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner participating virtually, a US official told AFP.

The official added that Zelensky had held “very productive and constructive discussions” with Witkoff and Kushner, who took part remotely while suffering from the flu.

“Ukraine brought forward new ideas and proposals,” the official said.

Trump saying at the White House that he wanted Zelensky to “make a deal” with Russia, which is ramping up strikes as a bitter winter looms.

Trump, who called on Zelensky to resign last week, also criticised the Ukrainian president for not accepting terms he said he had offered during an infamous televised row in the Oval Office in February 2025.

Ukraine reacted with dismay after Trump also waived sanctions against Russia.

The feud spiralled as Zelensky accused Trump of weakness, and then alleged that the United States was deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying the delivery of interceptor missiles.

Ukraine has also reported a reduction in speeds on Starshield, the US military satellite system it uses for battlefield communications and strikes on Russian-occupied territory.

Trump has denied ordering a reduction in speeds on Starshield after Elon Musk — whose company SpaceX developed it — said the order could only have come from the White House.

But the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday that it was indeed Musk who ordered the slowdown in the military-grade version of Starlink.

Witkoff’s meetings follow furious diplomatic efforts in Washington, Kyiv and Western capitals to calm the row.

Zelensky told US senators on Monday that “the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles” already paid for by European countries, while the shipment was waiting for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s signature.

Several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were awaiting US approval, he said.

Trump — whose Republican party faces tough midterm elections as fuel prices soar — has accused Zelensky of a lack of effort to resolve the conflict.

title: FAA certifies Boeing’s 737 MAX 10, clearing way for deliveries
author: Reuters
summary: FAA certifies Boeing’s 737 MAX 10, clearing way for deliveries
content:
EVERETT/WASHINGTON: The US Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday granted final approval to the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10, clearing the way ‌for the US planemaker to begin delivering the largest version of its best-selling airplane.

Boeing has said the MAX 10 will be a major driver of cash flow in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies that slowed the company’s timeline for the MAX 10. So far, airlines have ordered more than 1,550 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for 31% of Boeing’s outstanding 737 backlog, ​according to IBA, an aviation analytics consultancy.

The plane is critical to Boeing’s fight with Airbus for orders in the lucrative single-aisle jetliner market, with China’s COMAC ​C919 in a distant third place.

“We want to beat the Europeans, we want to beat the Chinese,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said ⁠Tuesday at Boeing’s plant in Everett, Washington, to tout the FAA certification.

“But if we want to continue to do that, I have to allow you all to certify ​aircraft faster,” Duffy said, a nod to his promise to streamline airplane certification.

Boeing has been trying to certify the 737 MAX 10 since the early 2020s. Boeing shares closed down about ​0.5%.

In July, the company opened a new production line at the Everett plant to increase 737 output, which it also assembles in nearby Renton.

Certification with Transport Canada and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency should be completed in “probably a couple months,” said Boeing Commercial Airplanes Senior Vice President Mike Sinnett, who oversees development programs.

Boeing can then deliver the first 737 MAX 10 to Canada-based airline WestJet, ​which is slated to happen early next year.

The largest MAX 10 can hold up to 230 passengers, compared with up to 195 for the MAX 9 and 160 for ​the MAX 7. However, the delays have helped European rival Airbus’ A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market.

US FAA tells airlines to exercise caution in Saudi Arabia flights

The bigger, higher-capacity plane is crucial to several airlines’ growth plans. Major customers ‌for the ⁠MAX 10 include United Airlines, Alaska Airlines, Ryanair, Delta Air Lines and American Airlines.

The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.

Boeing has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019 killed 346 people. Scrutiny of the company’s production and quality systems also increased after a January 2024 mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9.

The FAA in August approved the smaller 737 MAX 7 after a review that lasted more than eight ​years.The regulator required the MAX 10 to include ​significant improvements, including updates to the ⁠flight control system with an enhanced angle-of-attack sensor. Those will be applied to the existing fleet in the coming years.A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10.

Boeing disclosed another ​glitch in late September with the latest update of the 737 MAX’s navigation software, which threatened to further delay certification. ​However, the FAA determined ⁠it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane.

Some of the 737 MAX certification team will now help Boeing get certification of the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in ⁠2027.

Despite the ​long slog to certify the last 737 MAX variant, Boeing’s Chris Payne, who oversaw the plane’s certification program, ​struck an optimistic tone about speeding up the process.

“And what’s great is, you know, the administration’s working seamlessly with the FAA and with Boeing, and we’re all having the right dialog and conversations to be ​able to say what (does) the future look like and what (does) it need to look like,” he said.

title: Explainer: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections
author: Reuters
summary: Explainer: Three issues defining the 2026 US midterm elections
content:
President Donald Trump’s record-low popularity, voter frustration over the cost of living and a fierce immigration fight are shaping the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine whether Republicans keep control of Congress or Democrats gain the power to challenge his administration.

Republicans hold narrow majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to ​take control of each chamber.

The outcome will hinge on a relatively small number of competitive races, but the campaigns are being shaped nationally by Trump himself and voter ‌concerns over affordability and immigration.

Here is a look at the three issues defining the election:

The president has put himself front and center in the closing stretch of the campaign cycle despite his record-low popularity, with upcoming rallies in Florida, Iowa, Michigan and Texas. Trump’s approval rating has fallen to an all-time low 31%, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. Yet he has repeatedly urged voters to pretend he’s on the ballot, an effort that could motivate Democrats and independents to ​rally against his party despite the message being aimed at increasing turnout among Trump’s base.

Democrats have said Trump has broken his campaign promises to lower costs and end wars. They have ​vowed to tackle an affordability agenda to reduce Americans’ cost of living and hold the administration accountable for alleged corruption if voters give them control ⁠of either chamber.

Voters have consistently ranked the cost of living as the top issue this election cycle. Half of registered voters surveyed in a recent Reuters/Ipsos poll cited the cost of living as the most ​important factor in how they will vote. In the same poll, voters highlighted healthcare, gasoline, food and housing as the top household bills lawmakers should focus on.

Republicans’ top legislative achievement was a tax cut ​extension that slashed roughly $1 trillion in spending for Medicaid, the government health insurance program for low-income Americans, and other health programs. Democrats last year forced a government shutdown over a failed effort to extend expiring health subsidies that benefited 24 million Americans.

Gas prices have spiked since the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in February. The national average price of gas is $4.28 — $1.20 higher than it was a year ago, according to AAA. The average cost of ​diesel is $6.32 — a $2.70 increase from a year earlier.

Grocery costs are up 1.8% over the past year, according to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics data on consumer prices. Federal Housing Finance Agency data show ​home prices rose 2.1% over the past year. Congress passed a bipartisan housing bill earlier this year. It became law without Trump’s signature.

Preliminary data from the Department of Homeland Security showed a 95% drop in migrants apprehended ‌at the southwest ⁠border compared to former President Joe Biden’s administration. The agency said there have been no Border Patrol releases the entire fiscal year for the first time ever.

But fatal encounters with federal immigration agents have occurred in Maine, Minnesota and Texas. The backlash to the death of two US citizens in Minnesota pulled many Democrats in competitive primaries to the left this year, with some candidates calling for the impeachment of then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and others saying Immigration and Customs Enforcement should be abolished.

Democrats and Republicans sparred over immigration funding this year in a stalemate that forced Republicans to unilaterally pass a $70 billion ​bill to fund ICE and the Border Patrol ​for the remainder of Trump’s presidency. Republicans ⁠counter Democrats’ criticism by saying Democrats support open borders.

Federal immigration officials also raided the Washington home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota this month, drawing widespread condemnation from Democrats. A person familiar with the case against Omar told Reuters one potential aim of the investigation could be to strip her of US ​citizenship and deport her.

Artificial intelligence and data centers, cryptocurrency, abortion and Israel could also influence voters in individual races. In Ohio’s Senate race, ​for example, Democratic nominee Sherrod ⁠Brown has labeled Republican Senator Jon Husted the face of data centers, and the crypto super PAC Defend American Jobs has spent more than $46 million to reelect Husted over Brown, a former US senator who chaired the chamber’s Banking Committee.

In Maine’s Senate race, Democratic nominee Troy Jackson is hoping voters don’t forget that Republican Senator Susan Collins helped confirm Brett Kavanaugh to the Supreme Court, which later overturned the federal right to ⁠abortion. Collins is ​on the election ballot for the first time since the high court made abortion a state issue rather than a ​federal right.

In Michigan, Republican nominee Mike Rogers has indicated he would accept help from a pro-Israel super PAC that spent more than $30 million backing Democratic US Representative Haley Stevens in her unsuccessful primary against Abdul El-Sayed, who now faces Rogers in the ​general election. The group has already spent more than $280,000 on mailers against El-Sayed.

Earlier this week, Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection.

title: Real Madrid seek Super League setup payments from Premier League six
author: Reuters
summary: Real Madrid seek Super League setup payments from Premier League six
content:
Real Madrid are seeking contributions towards the setup costs of the failed European Super League project from ​the six Premier League clubs that withdrew shortly after its ‌launch, the Spanish side confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday.

The Athletic reported that the total costs could reach €80 million ($89.9 million). Real are seeking payments from ​Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham ​Hotspur.

The six were among nine of the competition’s 12 ⁠founding clubs that withdrew within three days of its launch ​in 2021 amid widespread opposition.

Real did not immediately confirm whether they ​were also seeking payments from the other three early leavers, AC Milan, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid said the six English clubs were liable ​for costs incurred in establishing the competition, which have so ​far been covered by Juventus, Barcelona and Real.

Tottenham declined to comment while the ‌other ⁠five Premier League clubs did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The Athletic reported that the clubs signed a shareholders’ agreement for the European Super League Company, the holding company ​behind the competition, ​although it is ⁠unclear whether the contract explicitly set out their liability for setup costs.

The Super League collapsed shortly ​after its launch following the withdrawal of the ​nine clubs.

Juventus ⁠subsequently pulled out of the project and Barcelona formally withdrew in February, leaving Real Madrid as its sole remaining founding club.

Real, UEFA ⁠and ​European Football Clubs announced an agreement ​of principles on February 11 aimed at resolving their Super League-related legal disputes.

title: Mir Raza Ali case: Father welcomes JIT recommendation, says protest will continue
author: Sanjay Sadhwani
summary: Mir Raza Ali case: Father welcomes JIT recommendation, says protest will continue
content:
KARACHI: Mir Raza Ali’s father, Mir Hussain, has welcomed the judicial commission’s recommendation to form a joint investigation team (JIT), saying his family had been demanding a JIT since the first day of the case, ARY News reported.

Mir Hussain thanked Sindh Chief Minister and Faryal Talpur, as well as the judge who headed the judicial commission, for the report.

He said the report had recommended the formation of a JIT and discussed the possibility of murder in the case. He added that the family had also submitted names for the proposed investigation team.

Mir Hussain said the judicial commission’s findings had brought police negligence to light and called for an investigation into the officers identified in the report.

He said the Sindh chief minister and a four-member cabinet committee would also take action on the report’s recommendations.

“We are not talking about what has been happening in Karachi for the past 70 to 75 years,” Mir Hussain said.

He added that the family’s protest would continue and that it would decide its future course of action once the JIT was officially announced.

Earlier, Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar said a special committee formed by the chief minister has begun reviewing recommendations made by the judicial commission investigating the Mir Raza Ali case.

Speaking to ARY News, Lanjar said the committee held its first meeting today, during which the judicial commission’s report was presented. Copies of the report were provided to all members of the subcommittee, he added.

The provincial home minister said police officers would face inquiries in line with the judicial commission’s recommendations, while officers found responsible for negligence and administrative incompetence would be suspended.

He further said a joint investigation team (JIT) would be formed on the judicial commission’s recommendation, provided there were no legal obstacles.

Lanjar said the committee would meet again to decide on the recommendations contained in the report.

title: Livestock sector records 43pc increase in animal exports: Dr.Naila
author: Web Desk, Aajiz Jamali
summary: Livestock sector records 43pc increase in animal exports: Dr.Naila
content:
Additional Director Livestock, Sargodha Region, Dr.Naila Maqsood, on Tuesday said the provincial government was taking measures to promote the livestock sector by providing a supportive environment and improved facilities to farmers.

She said Punjab’s livestock sector, including Sargodha’s contribution, had recorded a 43 per cent increase in animal exports with 400,000 animals prepared for export annually.

The initiative was expected to generate Rs.11 billion in earnings for rural livestock farmers, she added.

Dr.Naila attributed the progress to the Chief Minister’s Punjab Livestock Card Scheme, under which farmers were receiving Rs.27,000 per animal to meet feed and fodder expenses.

She said the provincial government had notified eight Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) compartments and planned to establish seven more during the current year, including one in Sargodha to facilitate exports to China, Europe and the United States.

A total of 129,581 animals reared under the Livestock Card Scheme had been exported, she added.

The government also planned to establish five meat-processing plants and five modern slaughterhouses, along with meat-packing facilities and commercial and corporate feedlots, she said.

Dr.Naila said Rs.19 billion in financing subsidies would be provided for integrated investments across the livestock value chain while private investment of Rs.65 billion was expected in the meat sector.

She further said Punjab would establish its first Foot-and-Mouth Disease vaccine production unit under a public-private partnership, involving private investment of Rs28 billion.

Giving district-wise export figures, she said 20,000 animals had been exported from Lahore, 24,297 from Bahawalpur,12,529 from Faisalabad, 21,000 from Gujranwala and Gujrat, 27,000 from Multan, 22,000 from Sargodha and 2,661 from Sahiwal.

Under the Livestock Connect system, the government had established direct links with 1,725 fattening farms, 20 export slaughterhouses, 88 meat exporters and 34 meat traders, she said.

The additional director said the number of rural women livestock farmers registered under the Livestock Card Scheme had increased from 90 to 1,107.

title: New heart study confirms human bodies can handle Mars gravity after spaceflight
author: Kumail Shah
summary: New heart study confirms human bodies can handle Mars gravity after spaceflight
content:
A new study suggests that sending people to Mars could be more achievable than once thought. Researchers from Northwestern Medicine, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and UTHealth Houston followed 13 astronauts during six-month stays on the International Space Station.

The study, published inthe Journal Circulation, is the first to examine how the human heart responds to Martian gravity after a long period of weightlessness.

One of NASA’s main worries when planning missions to Mars is whether astronauts’ hearts can handle moving from deep space’s microgravity to Mars’s gravity, which is about one-third as strong as Earth’s.

In the past, astronauts coming back to Earth often had orthostatic hypotension, which is a sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up. This causes dizziness and lightheadedness because being in space reduces muscle and heart mass. But in this study, most astronauts avoided these problems by following NASA’s Exercise Countermeasures program.

To stay healthy in space, the astronauts worked out for up to two hours each day. Their routine included 30 to 45 minutes of endurance training and 60 to 75 minutes of resistance exercises. Dr. James Thomas, a cardiology professor at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine and the study’s senior author, said these results give strong reason to think astronauts can go to Mars and work well there.

Dr. Thomas worked with Dr. Benjamin Levine and Dr. Michael Bungo to study ultrasound heart scans, called echocardiograms, taken before, during, and after each mission. The astronauts scanned each other every few weeks while in space, with Dr. Thomas guiding them live from Earth, sometimes as early as 3 a.m.

During their first two weeks in space, the astronauts’ hearts pumped less blood and filled less than usual. However, their heart function slowly returned to normal as the mission went on.

After returning to Earth, researchers simulated arrival on Mars by tilting the astronauts 22 degrees upward while they lay down, which shifted blood toward their lower bodies. The tests showed no major heart problems, meaning their hearts handled the simulated Martian gravity as well as standing upright on Earth before the mission.

title: NADRA warns overseas Pakistanis against unauthorized agents
author: Web Desk
summary: NADRA warns overseas Pakistanis against unauthorized agents
content:
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has urged overseas Pakistanis not to share their personal information with unauthorized individuals or organizations claiming to be affiliated with the authority.

NADRA said it had no approved consultants, agents or dealers to process identity documents or submit online applications on its behalf.

It said services for overseas Pakistanis were available through NADRA Registration Centers and counters established at Pakistani embassies abroad.

A list of these facilities can be found on the authority’s official website:https://www.nadra.gov.pk/nadraStatistics

NADRA said its online services were available exclusively through the Pak ID mobile app and its official websites ending in gov.pk.

It urged overseas Pakistanis to remain vigilant and avoid sharing personal information with anyone falsely claiming to represent NADRA.

title: PM Shehbaz arrives in Peshawar for apex committee meeting, security briefing
author: Shahid Hamid
summary: Prime minister is also expected to address a grand jirga during his visit
content:
Prime minister is also expected to address a grand jirga during his visit

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Peshawar on Thursday to attend an apex committee meeting on the law and order situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), with a major development package for the province also expected to be announced during his visit, sources said.

According to sources, the prime minister was scheduled to receive a briefing on the security situation in the province and participate in the apex committee meeting, which will discuss peace and stability in K-P.

Members of the provincial advisory council arrived at Governor House to meet PM Shehbaz, while relevant officials of the Regional Development Secretariat were also present there, sources added.

The prime minister is also expected to address a grand jirga during his visit.

The visit marked Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s first trip to Peshawar since theimpositionof emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, which resulted in the suspension of the provincial government led by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).

The federal government imposed the measures under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, citing a deterioration in the security situation, an increase in terrorist attacks, and what it described as the provincial administration’s failure to cooperate effectively in counter-terrorism efforts.

Under the new arrangement, executive powers were transferred to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, assisted by an advisory council, while emergency measures were imposed in 12 districts. The PTI rejected the federal government’s position and opposed the move.

The decision followed weeks of tensions between the Centre and the PTI-led provincial administration, alongside negotiations aimed at securing agreement on a joint strategy against terrorism.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the federal government had made repeated attempts to obtain the provincial government’s cooperation before resorting to the constitutional measures. Prime Minister Shehbaz also said the government had been left withno alternativeafter negotiations failed to produce an agreement.

Thefirst provincial Apex Committeemeeting following the imposition of governor’s rule was held at Governor House on October 12, co-chaired by Governor Kundi and Interior Minister Naqvi. The meeting reviewed the security situation and counter-terrorism measures, with participants agreeing to strengthen the police and Counter-Terrorism Department through additional equipment, vehicles, weapons and manpower. The forum also called for coordinated action by relevant institutions to restore peace and improve law and order.

title: St.Louis down Columbus to win US Open Cup
author: AFP
summary: Edelman’s decisive kick gives his side a 5-3 shoot-out victory
content:
Edelman’s decisive kick gives his side a 5-3 shoot-out victory

St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday, defeating Major League Soccer rivals Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the US Open Cup.

Daniel Edelman stroked in the decisive spot-kick to secure a 5-3 shoot-out win for St. Louis after the two teams finished locked at 0-0 after extra-time in Columbus.

Substitute goalkeeper Ben Lundt was another hero for St. Louis, saving Columbus's opening penalty from Santiago Rodriguez in the shoot-out.

It was a case of history repeating itself for St. Louis's Edelman, who scored the winning penalty in a shoot-out to eliminate Columbus during the 2024 MLS postseason.

"Thankfully I've been there before and it's all about the process when you step up," Edelman said afterwards. "You just have to believe, have a good mindset and focus on how you strike the ball, which is exactly what I did."

Edelman marked his winning penalty by sprinting the length of the pitch to celebrate with St. Louis supporters at Crew's ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

The US Open Cup – the oldest annual team tournament in the United States which was first played in 1913-1914 – marks the first silverware won by St. Louis, who joined MLS as an expansion team in 2019.

"It's the first trophy for me and a lot of guys and for the city," Edelman said. "For us as a team it's phenomenal to have this night and have this trophy."

title: MotoGP bids farewell to Phillip Island
author: AFP
summary: Riders prepare for an emotional final weekend at the iconic circuit
content:
Riders prepare for an emotional final weekend at the iconic circuit

Seven-time world champion Marc Marquez admits it will be "emotional" this weekend as one of MotoGP's most iconic circuits at Phillip Island hosts its last race after nearly three decades.

The picturesque and often windswept track, some two hours outside of Melbourne, has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 and a favourite among the riders given its waterfront location and demanding layout.

Promoter MotoGP Sports Entertainment wanted to broaden its appeal and shift it to Melbourne's Albert Park, which hosts the Australian Formula One.

The Victorian state government was adamant it should remain at Phillip Island.

With negotiations breaking down, South Australia stepped in and secured the race for six years from 2027 in Adelaide -- the first MotoGP to be held in a city‑centre location.

"Phillip Island is an extraordinary circuit. Racing here for the last time will be emotional," said Ducati's Marquez, who heads into the weekend two points behind Aprilia's Jorge Martin in the championship standings.

"It is a track with a unique, breathtaking layout. Here I won one of my first races with Ducati and we are motivated to do well, ready to fight right away for the positions that matter."

The venue has seen some of the Spaniard's most impressive rides -- he is a four-time winner -- and also some of his worst moments including a huge high-speed crash with Johann Zarco in 2018.

Teammate Francesco Bagnaia has never stood on the top step of the Phillip Island podium.

But the 2022 and 2023 races, where he finished third and second respectively, were vitally important to his title-winning exploits and he too is sad to see it go.

"It will be the last time on this track, a circuit where I haven't managed to win yet, but which holds an incredible charm, an extraordinary layout, and pure adrenaline," he said.

With five rounds to go, the title fight has effectively become a three-way battle between Martin, reigning champion Marquez and Marco Bezzecchi, who won the last race in Indonesia to stay in touch.

Aprilia's Bezzecchi is 44 points behind Marquez and 50 clear of fourth-placed Ai Ogura.

"We arrive in Australia with the gaps in the riders' standings even tighter, so we have to keep working and keep faith in what everyone at Aprilia and the team is doing," said Martin.

"I'm confident that my team and I will do an excellent job and give this circuit the send-off it deserves."

Marquez and Martin both missed last year's Australian race with injuries, and Spain's Raul Fernandez grabbed his chance to surge to a maiden MotoGP victory.

Currently seventh in the standings, Fernandez is equally dismayed at the race leaving Phillip Island.

"I will cry a little bit," he said. "Not because I got my first MotoGP victory here but also because I always enjoy it a lot coming to Phillip Island -- it is super nice.

"There were so many interesting races in the past here, not just in MotoGP, also in Moto2 and Moto3, so it's a track that everybody will miss a little bit."

title: Bangladesh crash out of tri-series after Afghanistan defeat
author: Sports Desk
summary: Rahmat Shah’s unbeaten 67 guides Afghanistan into final against Zimbabwe
content:
Rahmat Shah’s unbeaten 67 guides Afghanistan into final against Zimbabwe

Bangladesh crashed out of the ODI tri-series after suffering a crushing seven-wicket defeat to Afghanistan, whose comfortable victory secured their place in Friday’s final against Zimbabwe.

Needing to win by more than 40 runs to qualify on net run-rate, Bangladesh were bowled out for 160 in 41.2 overs after electing to bat first at Sharjah Cricket Stadium.

Afghanistan chased down the target with 87 balls to spare, reaching 161-3 in 35.3 overs, as captain Rahmat Shah led the way with an unbeaten 67.

The Afghans will face Zimbabwe in the final after already thrashing them by 158 runs in the group stage. Bangladesh, meanwhile, had also suffered a 99-run defeat against Zimbabwe.

Parvez Hossain Emon offered the main resistance for Bangladesh, scoring a career-best 70 in his first one-day international in more than a year. But his fighting innings could not prevent another batting collapse.

Leg-spinner Rashid Khan claimed four wickets for 31 runs to dismantle the lower order, while fast bowler Yamin Ahmadzai struck twice in the second over to leave Bangladesh reeling.

Opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim fell for one before Soumya Sarkar was dismissed for a duck on consecutive deliveries, both undone by loose shots.

Azmatullah Omarzai then removed Najmul Hossain Shanto for 15 and captain Towhid Hridoy for a duck in the space of three deliveries, reducing Bangladesh to 28-4 in the seventh over.

Emon, recalled to the squad after Liton Das was injured, attempted to rebuild alongside Saif Hassan, who provided valuable resistance amid the early collapse.

The pair added 93 runs for the fifth wicket before Saif fell for 41 while attempting an attacking shot against Mohammad Nabi.

Emon reached his second half-century in just his fourth ODI, striking five fours and two sixes to give Bangladesh hope of posting a competitive total.

But Rashid triggered another collapse, with Bangladesh losing their final five wickets for just 39 runs.

Despite the modest target, Bangladesh had a slim mathematical chance of defending their total by dismissing Afghanistan for fewer than 119 runs.

Fast bowler Taskin Ahmed briefly raised hopes by removing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for six with a sharp inswinger before dismissing Sediqullah Atal for four, leaving Afghanistan at 39-2 in the seventh over.

However, Bangladesh failed to capitalise on the early breakthroughs as Mustafizur Rahman and Shoriful Islam struggled to contain the chase.

Debutant mystery spinner Aliss Al Islam also went wicketless, conceding 47 runs in 8.3 overs.

Rahmat steadied the innings with a 56-run partnership with Ibrahim Zadran, who scored 34, before adding an unbeaten 66 with Hashmatullah Shahidi, who finished on 36.

The partnerships ensured Afghanistan reached their target comfortably and ended Bangladesh’s hopes of reaching the final.

Taskin finished with two wickets for 36 runs, while Mustafizur claimed one for 32.

title: Govt, JI negotiating committees to meet over petroleum levy tomorrow
author: Naeem Asghar
summary: JI's Baloch says protests will begin again tomorrow, and that negotiations and protests will continue 'side by side'
content:
JI's Baloch says protests will begin again tomorrow, and that negotiations and protests will continue 'side by side'

The government and Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) negotiating committees are set to meet in Islamabad on Friday to discuss the abolition of the petroleum levy, as the party prepares to resume nationwide protests over fuel prices, JI Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch said on Thursday.

Baloch said the meeting, scheduled for October 23, was arranged following a telephone conversation between Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and himself.

He added that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was also expected to meet JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman during the negotiations.

Baloch said the party would also hold nationwide protests on Friday to demand the abolition of the petroleum levy.

“Negotiations and protests will continue side by side. The people must receive relief and economic activity must continue,” he said.

The party has maintained that it will continue its protest campaign until the government agrees to withdraw the levy.

JI first launched sit-ins on August 16 in Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta against the petroleum levy, rising fuel prices and inflation. The party accused the government of shifting the burden of its economic policies onto ordinary citizens and demanded the abolition of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices.

The party held a nationwide shutdown strike on September 3, after which the government and JI agreed to formtechnical committeesto examine proposals for reducing the levy and fuel prices. JI subsequentlysubmitted six proposalsto the government during the first round of negotiations in Islamabad on September 7.

However, successive rounds of talks failed to produce an agreement, with the government citing economic constraints and pressure under the International Monetary Fund programme, while JI insisted that the levy should be abolished.

On September 20, the partylaunched a long marchtowards Islamabad, beginning with a train journey from Karachi. The caravan travelled to Sukkur before continuing towards Multan, where JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman addressed supporters.

Read:Minister defends daily fuel pricing formula

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif subsequently telephoned Rehman and asked him to postpone the march, offering to meet the party leadership after returning from abroad to discuss relief for the public.

Rehman said the party had agreed to give the prime minister an opportunity to hold talks but wouldnot abandonits demands. JI suspended the train march at the prime minister’s request, with its workers remaining in Multan pending further negotiations.

The government and JI continued discussions in the following weeks, but the dispute over the levy remained unresolved. The party has since maintained that any meeting between its chief and the prime minister must focus on the complete abolition of the charge.

The petroleum levy is a federal charge imposed on petroleum products and forms part of the taxes collected by the government through fuel sales. It is separate from the underlying price of the fuel and contributes to the cost paid by consumers at petrol pumps.

JI argues that the levy adds to the financial burden on households already facing inflation and higher transport costs. The party has linked its demand for the levy’s abolition to its wider campaign for lower fuel prices and relief from the rising cost of living.

The government, meanwhile, has said it is working to provide relief to consumers while managing economic constraints under the IMF programme. The disagreement has persisted despite several rounds of negotiations, with JI demanding the complete withdrawal of the levy rather than a limited relief package.

title: Manchester United thrashed as Arsenal snatch Bayern draw
author: AFP
summary: Como pile pressure on Michael Carrick with a 4-1 rout
content:
Como pile pressure on Michael Carrick with a 4-1 rout

Manchester United were hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday as the pressure increased on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, while a late Declan Rice equaliser earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

Elsewhere, Real Madrid thumped RB Leipzig 4-1 and there were also notable victories for Inter Milan, Aston Villa and Real Betis.

The most remarkable scoreline, though, came in driving rain on the banks of Lake Como, where United suffered their joint-heaviest loss in the Champions League in the last 30 years.

Nico Paz scored twice for Cesc Fabregas's Como, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon getting their other goals. This was a second 4-1 home win in this season's competition for the tournament debutants.

Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back at the death for United, but they are now seven games without a win in all competitions.

The Red Devils have just one win in the Premier League this season and have now suffered back-to-back losses in Europe. Carrick's position risks becoming untenable.

"I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said.

"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all," he admitted.

Last season's beaten finalists Arsenal have seven points from a possible nine after Rice struck in the 82nd minute to earn a draw in Munich.

Bukayo Saka went off injured early on but his replacement Eberechi Eze fired Arsenal into the lead, only for Alphonso Davies to level before the interval.

Harry Kane set up that goal with a magnificent pass and then gave Bayern the lead from a second-half penalty, his 10th strike this season in all competitions.

But Arsenal hit back as Bayern registered a second straight Champions League stalemate.

"We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game," Kane told broadcaster DAZN.

"Probably a draw was a fair result overall... There's a lot of games and we've got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on."

Jose Mourinho's Real are one of five teams with three wins from three in this season's Champions League, as goals either side of half-time from Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler set them on their way at the Bernabeu.

Kylian Mbappe made it 12 goals in 12 games this season for Real before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back, but Yan Diomande completed Real's victory with a spectacular volley against his former club.

"We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible -- we've won three and there are five to go," Mbappe told Movistar.

Villa also have a perfect record after three games, as they won 3-1 at home to Viking Stavanger with Ross Barkley's opener being followed by Emiliano Buendia's penalty and Henrik Heggheim's own goal.

Peter Christiansen got one back for the Norwegian champions who are still looking for their first win.

Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto's late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points.

Betis have maximum points as an Isco penalty handed them a 1-0 win over Feyenoord in Seville.

Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 in Belgium as Hans Vanaken, Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs all found the net.

Victor Osimhen sealed a 4-2 victory for Galatasaray away to his old side Lille in France, after earlier efforts from Yunus Akgun and Aleksey Batrakov and a Nabil Bentaleb own goal.

Teenager Soriba Diaoune got both goals for Lille, who have lost three out of three.

LASK of Austria have their first points after a fine 3-2 victory over Sporting in Lisbon.

Luis Suarez scored twice for Sporting, including an early penalty, but Christoph Lang, Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek all netted in between for the visitors.

Reigning champions PSG are top of the 36-team standings after beating Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the French side confirmed Wednesday that star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in that game.

He will undergo surgery in the coming days amid doubts as to whether he will play again this season.

title: Two killed, eight injured in attack on airport in Saudi oil city Dammam
author: Reuters
summary: US orders some diplomats, family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
content:
US orders some diplomats, family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes

Two people were killed, and eight were injured in an attack on Wednesday evening on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil city of Dammam, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday.

Those killed were a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, the authority said. The injuries ranged from minor to serious. Damage was being assessed, it added.

Airport operations had resumed, and air traffic had returned to normal, the authority said.

Meanwhile, The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials toldReuters.

The order came amid attacks in Saudi Arabia that killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam, and two people were killed in a drone attack on an oil field.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a post on X that the department ordered the departure of "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only" amid attacks by the Houthis in Yemen on civilian targets in the country.

Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months after many were pulled out when Tehran launched attacks on US facilities after the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

Read:2 killed after Saudi air defenses intercept drone targeting Aramco oil field

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," Pigott said.

Four US officials toldReutersthat US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave. Pigott did not address changes to other missions outside Saudi Arabia.

The latest withdrawals follow an escalation of the fighting in Yemen, opening another front ​in the regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli ⁠war on Iran. The wider conflict has snarled global energy trade and hurt Gulf economies.

Houthis strike Yemen’s Al-Rayyan airport for fourth timein hours: Army

Yemen’s army said on early Thursday that the Houthi group targeted Al-Rayyan International Airport in the city of Mukalla, the capital of Hadramout province, for the fourth time within hours.

The army’s official spokesman, Maj. Gen. Majed al-Nuzaili, said the “Houthi terrorist militia targeted Al-Rayyan International Airport in Mukalla for the fourth time,” according toSeptember Net, a website affiliated with Yemen’s Defence Ministry.

In a statement, Nuzaili said that “targeting airports aims to impose a blockade on the Yemeni people,” the website reported. Al-Rayyan is one of Yemen’s most important civilian airports, serving millions of people in Hadramout and other provinces.

The Houthis had not immediately commented on the attack.

Two killed after Saudi air defenses intercept drone targeting Aramco oil field

Two foreign nationalswere killedand two others injured Wednesday after Saudi air defenses intercepted a drone attempting to target a facility at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field in the country’s Eastern Province, the Energy Ministry said.

A ministry official said Saudi air defenses intercepted the drone as it attempted to strike one of the facilities at the oil field,accordingto the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

Debris from the interception sparked a fire in a vehicle belonging to a contractor working at the field, outside the facility’s perimeter, the official said.

Read more:Oil rises as US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions

The incident did not affect operations at the oil field, the ministry added.

The official identified the two fatalities as Philippine and Nepalese nationals, while the injured were Pakistani and Indian nationals.

Relevant authorities responded to the incident and took the necessary measures, according to the statement.

title: Iran's IRGC Navy says seven vessels hit, warns US of wider response
author: Reuters
summary: Trump says US ‘not negotiating’ with Iran, something will happen ‘fairly soon’
content:
Trump says US ‘not negotiating’ with Iran, something will happen ‘fairly soon’

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Thursday that it had targeted four ships in the northern part of the Arabian Gulf that it said were transferring oil cargoes from one vessel to another.

The IRGC’s naval forces said in a statement that "fires were still burning on the targeted ships." It added that the four vessels had been spotted transferring oil between ships and were targeted simultaneously for sailing along “unauthorised routes.”

The IRGC accused the US of “encouraging ships to cross a maritime passage planted with mines,” saying this was leading to an “increase in maritime incidents.”

The statement warned Washington that if the US continued with this approach, the scope of Iran’s response “would also include American bases in the region.”

Iran's IRGC Navy says seven vessels hit, warns US of wider response

IRGC Navy said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

The IRGC added that three more vessels collided with mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases.

Trump says US ‘not negotiating’ with Iran, something will happen ‘fairly soon’

US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that Washington is not negotiating with Iran, adding that “something one way or the other” will happen “fairly soon.”

“No, I think we’re not negotiating,” Trump told reporters upon returning from a rally in South Carolina. “We are going to have something one way or the other that’ll happen fairly soon.”

“Most people seem to think it’s after the election, and we’re going to see what happens,” he added.

Earlier, during his remarks at the rally, Trump said the US could end its war with Iran now but wants to ensure that the outcome is lasting.

“It’ll end very soon. We could leave now, but we want to make sure it lasts for a long time,” he said.

He claimed the US had defeated Iran militarily and financially, adding that Tehran would “never have a nuclear weapon.”

Read:CDF Munir meets senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continues diplomatic push to end conflict

His remarks came as TheNew York Timesreported that the US and Israeli militaries have developed plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, citing US officials and others briefed on the deliberations.

The report said it is far from certain that Trump will approve the strikes, noting that he has repeatedly vetoed plans to return to major combat this year.

A White House official told theTimesthat the administration does not comment on military plans “that may or may not exist.”

US, Israel develop plans for renewed strikes on Iran after midterm elections: report

The US and Israeli militaries have developed plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the US midterm elections, with preparations advancing for a potential short but intensive campaign, TheNew York Timesreported on Wednesday.

Citing US officials and other people briefed on the deliberations, the newspaper reported that the two militaries have stepped up exercises, including flights over Iraq to practice strike maneuvers.

Potential targets could include Iran’s nuclear facilities, missile and drone arsenal, and energy infrastructure, according to the report.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week to discuss possible new strikes, the newspaper reported. Plans to target Iran’s nuclear program could include a strike on Pickaxe Mountain, a deeply buried site, according to theTimes.

The report said it is far from certain that Trump will approve the strikes, noting that he has repeatedly vetoed plans to return to major combat this year.

Iran threatens to target US political assets, infrastructure if new war erupts

Iran would consider US political assets and infrastructure belonging to countries participating in a new war against it as “legitimate targets” if Iranian officials were assassinated or civilians killed, a senior Iranian security official warned on Wednesday, according to theFars NewsAgency.

The Tehran-based official said Iran assumes that the US and Israel will launch another attack and considers Washington’s diplomatic gestures “unreliable.”

The official said this perception had intensified following remarks by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Athens, which Tehran interpreted as giving a historical and civilisational justification for Washington’s war against Iran.

According to the official, Iranian political and intellectual leaders have increasingly concluded that US Middle East policy is directed by Israel, which they believe is preventing Washington from pursuing a diplomatic solution.

The official claimed that Israel takes priority in US President Donald Trump’s regional policies.

Read more:US-Iran talks continue through Pakistan, Qatar: Iranian FM

Iran already considers itself at war with the US and views Washington’s economic and naval blockade, along with restrictions on Iranian airspace, as a continuation of the military aggression that began on February 28, the official said.

He added that growing pressure from different segments of Iranian society was pushing authorities toward “decisive action” to break the blockade under what Tehran considers its right to self-defence.

According to the official, Iran has instructed various operational units that, in the event of another large-scale conflict involving the assassination of Iranian officials and the killing of civilians, it would consider US political assets and the infrastructure of countries participating in the war as “legitimate targets.”

The warning comes amid heightened tensions between Tehran and Washington over the US naval blockade and restrictions on maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Oil rises as US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid escalating tensions
author: Reuters
summary: Brent crude futures rise $1.29, or 1.2%, to $110.11 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures rise $1.29, or 1.2%, to $110.11 a barrel

Oil prices rose on Thursday as more attacks by the Houthis in Saudi ‌Arabia prompted the United States to order some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in the Kingdom.

Brent crude futures rose $1.29, or 1.2%, to $110.11 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 97 cents, or 1%, to $98.12. Brent had settled largely ​unchanged on Wednesday, while WTI had eased 67 cents.

The US State Department plans to withdraw family members ​from a number of other US missions in the region, US officials toldReuters.

Yemen's Houthis struck several targets on Wednesday, with at least one person killed and eight more wounded at a ​civilian airport in Dammam, and two people killed in a drone attack on a Saudi oil field.

Explosions were ​also heard in Sirik in southern Iran, Iranian media reported on Wednesday, saying the nature and origin of the explosions were unknown.

On Wednesday, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told theFinancial Timesthat Iran was fully prepared to defend itself, and President ​Masoud Pezeshkian told state media the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.

There were at ​least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks, Kpler data showed, while LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting ‌tankers ⁠well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional loadings.

title: Dengue cases surge sharply across K-P
author: Shahida Parveen
summary: Province reports 1,510 infections in October, with Kohat emerging as the worst-hit district
content:
Province reports 1,510 infections in October, with Kohat emerging as the worst-hit district

Dengue virus infections are rising sharply across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, with 1,510 cases reported during October so far, including 99 new infections confirmed in the past 24 hours, according to the provincial health department.

The department's daily dengue situation report identified Kohat as the worst-affected district, reporting 975 cases during October, followed by Peshawar with 209 cases. The total number of confirmed dengue infections in the province has reached 4,091 this year, while one death has been reported in Dera Ismail Khan.

According to the district-wise report for 2026, Kohat and Peshawar remain the main hotspots, although infections have also been reported in Bannu, Charsadda, Haripur, Abbottabad, Hangu, Nowshera and several other districts.

The province currently has 144 active dengue cases, with Kohat accounting for 80. Bannu has 24 active cases, Peshawar 18, Hangu nine, Charsadda seven, DI Khan three, Nowshera two and Lakki Marwat one.

Kohat's situation remains particularly concerning, with 2,567 cases recorded since the beginning of the year. These include 42 cases in July, 387 in August, 1,116 in September and 975 in October, reflecting the continued spread of the virus in the district.

In Peshawar, the annual tally has reached 566, including 75 cases in August, 144 in September and 209 in October.

Other districts have also reported a significant number of infections. Bannu recorded 81 cases during October, followed by Charsadda with 37, Haripur with 34, Abbottabad with 21, and Hangu and Nowshera with 20 each.

The report showed 17 cases in Karak, 14 in DI Khan, 11 in Lakki Marwat, 10 in Bajaur, seven each in Swabi and Lower Chitral, three in Malakand and one in Mardan. Two cases were reported in Battagram, while no infections were recorded in Upper Chitral.

Several districts, including Shangla, Upper Dir, Upper Kohistan, Kolai-Palas, Lower and Upper South Waziristan, Lower and Upper Kurram and Torghar, reported no cases this year.

The monthly figures indicate a marked increase in infections since August. The province recorded 115 cases from January through May, 90 in June, 111 in July, 573 in August, 1,692 in September and 1,510 so far in October.

Health officials have urged residents to take preventive measures to curb the spread of dengue. People have been advised to prevent water from accumulating in homes, streets and neighbourhoods, keep water containers covered and eliminate potential mosquito breeding sites.

Residents experiencing fever, severe headaches, body aches, joint pain or other suspected symptoms have been advised to seek prompt medical attention.

The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Wednesday restrained the police from arresting Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suraiya Bibi under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance and suspended the administration's notification sealing her official residence.

A two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Muhammad Fahim Wali heard the writ petition filed by the deputy speaker through her counsel, Yasar Khattak Advocate. The court issued notices to the chief secretary, inspector general of police and other relevant authorities, directing them to submit their replies by the next date of hearing.

Counsel for the petitioner told the court that Suraiya Bibi was allotted the official residence in 2024 in her capacity as deputy speaker. Following the imposition of emergency and Governor's Rule in the province on October 11, police raided her residence on October 14 and sealed the premises, an action he described as illegal.

Khattak argued that even under emergency and Governor's Rule, the official residence of the deputy speaker could not be sealed without fulfilling legal requirements. He sought orders restraining her arrest under 3-MPO and directing the authorities to de-seal the residence, contending that the moves amounted to political victimisation.

The lawyer further submitted that both the speaker and deputy speaker continue to hold their constitutional offices under the law until a new assembly is formed, and any such action against them is ultra vires the Constitution and the law.

After hearing the arguments, the bench stayed Suraiya Bibi's arrest under 3-MPO and suspended the notification sealing her official residence pending further proceedings.

title: Governor halts supply of hazardous wheat
author: Ahtesham Bashir
summary: Inquiry finds flood-damaged grain at Azakhel godown unfit for human consumption
content:
Inquiry finds flood-damaged grain at Azakhel godown unfit for human consumption

A high-level meeting chaired by Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Wednesday reviewed an inquiry into the supply of substandard and potentially hazardous wheat from the Azakhel wheat godown to flour mills across the province.

The Governor Inspection Team presented its detailed findings during the session. Team Chairman Mukhtiar Ahmad informed the governor that the team had thoroughly inspected the sprawling 150-kanal facility at Azakhel. Six godowns located in two blocks of the complex were found to have been inundated by floodwater. Samples of the damaged wheat were dispatched to the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (PCSIR) laboratory for analysis. The laboratory report declared the flood-affected grain harmful to human health and unfit for human consumption.

According to the inquiry, critical protective measures to shield the godown from floodwater had never been implemented. Despite repeated flood alerts issued by the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), authorities failed to adopt even basic precautionary steps. After the flooding occurred, the Food Department neglected to constitute a technical assessment committee to evaluate the quality and safety of the stored wheat. The report explicitly recommended disciplinary action against the officers found responsible for this negligence.

Governor Kundi questioned why, despite the site's history of repeated flooding, a proper protective wall had never been constructed around the godown. Officials briefed him that existing gaps and holes in the incomplete barrier allowed rainwater and floodwater to pour directly into the storage blocks, spoiling large quantities of wheat.

Further discrepancies came to light: the Food Department's official stock records contained no entry acknowledging the flood-damaged wheat, and no scientific testing of the affected stocks had been carried out by the department itself prior to the Governor Inspection Team's intervention.

In clear and firm directions, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi ordered an immediate halt to the supply of any wheat deemed hazardous to health from the Azakhel facility to flour mills. He emphasized the urgent need to safeguard remaining wheat reserves, enforce strict quality controls on food commodities, and fix individual responsibility for lapses that placed public health at risk.

The governor stressed that protecting essential food stocks is a fundamental responsibility of the provincial administration. He directed relevant departments to ensure that all future storage facilities are adequately protected against natural disasters and that transparent record-keeping and independent quality assessments become standard practice. Officials were instructed to submit a follow-up compliance report detailing the steps taken to implement the recommendations of the inquiry.
