title: LHC quashes case over unproven allegation
author: Our Correspondent
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that a person cannot be prosecuted under Section 182 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) merely because an allegation or information provided by them could not be substantiated.

Justice Ghulam Sarwar Nehung, in a written judgment, held that the prosecution must establish that the information was knowingly false and provided with mala fide intent.

The judge observed that failure to prove an allegation and proving it false were two distinct matters.

The court held that a person providing information in good faith could not be convicted under the provision merely because it subsequently proved incorrect.

It further ruled that a written complaint by the public servant concerned was mandatory for initiating proceedings under Section 182 of the PPC. Proceedings initiated without such a complaint did not fulfil the legal requirements, the court observed.

The judge also held that a show-cause notice must be issued to the person concerned, giving them an opportunity to explain their position before proceedings were initiated.

Allowing a petition filed by Muhammad Shahid, the high court set aside the subordinate courts' orders dated February 26 and March 24, 2025, and quashed the criminal proceedings against him under Section 182 of the PPC.

The proceedings had been initiated after an error in the identification card number recorded in the property tax record was corrected.

A 12-year-old girl died allegedly after being tortured by her employer, while a nine-year-old girl sustained injuries in a separate incident.

In the first incident, a 12-year-old girl, identified as Zainab, allegedly died after being assaulted by her employer at a house on Khalid Road in the jurisdiction of A Division police station.

According to her mother, Zainab had been working at the house of a woman named Farhanda for the past 18 months for a monthly salary of Rs4,000.

She said that after 10pm on the night of the incident, Farhanda called her and told her that the girl was unwell and asked her to come to the house immediately without bringing anyone along.

The mother said she was unable to afford even the Rs100 rickshaw fare and had to walk for nearly two hours to reach the house.

She alleged that the woman repeatedly refused to let her speak to her daughter over the phone.

Upon reaching the house, she found Zainab lying on the floor, with a wooden stick lying nearby. The woman and her son were reportedly not present at the house at the time.

The victim's mother said her brother called police. The police collected evidence and shifted the body to a hospital for a post-mortem examination.

Farhanda, her son Ali Haider and her husband, Riffaqat, have been nominated in the case.

Zainab's father had died six months ago, while her mother works at a brick kiln.

The family's financial difficulties had compelled the girl to work as a domestic helper, earning Rs4,000 a month, her mother said.

In a separate incident two days earlier, a nine-year-old girl, identified as Iman Fatima, allegedly suffered a fractured arm after being assaulted by a married couple in Gujjar Town, within the jurisdiction of Sadar police station.

In a video statement, the girl alleged that her employer repeatedly applied a heated metal rod to sensitive parts of her body. She said neighbours intervened after hearing her screams and helped rescue her.

According to sources, the woman, identified as Zunaira, and her husband, Waris, both work for the police department. Police have registered a case and initiated legal proceedings.

District Police Officer Bilal Zafar Sheikh has taken notice of the incident and constituted a team under the supervision of the SP Investigation.

Police said further action would be taken in light of the post-mortem report and available evidence. Advocate High Court Hamid Khan said the incident of violence against a domestic worker in Sheikhupura was the second such case reported in the city within a few days.

He said the failure to enforce the law and ensure justice, coupled with influential individuals escaping punishment, was contributing to an increase in such incidents.

He stressed that the state must take strict measures to prevent such crimes and ensure that perpetrators think twice before committing similar acts in the future.

Suspect Riffaqat has been arrested following strict notice taken by Sheikhupura District Police Officer (DPO) Bilal Sheikh.

The DPO said strict legal action would be taken against the suspects and that no leniency would be shown towards them.

The Lahore Gymkhana Club's chairman has acknowledged that the Rs5,000 annual rent for more than 100 acres of prime state land is inadequate, suggesting it should be raised to at least Rs10 million, prompting a Punjab Assembly committee to question how successive governments had allowed the arrangement to continue for decades without proper valuation or oversight.

The special committee questioned the failure of governments to secure appropriate return from over 100 acres of prime state land leased to the club for the nominal annual rent of Rs5,000.

The Punjab Assembly Special Committee No. 6, chaired by MPA Samiullah Khan, on Wednesday sought to establish how such a concession had continued for decades without proper valuation, government oversight or scrutiny of the lease terms.

The committee was informed that the land's estimated value ranged from Rs76 billion to Rs218 billion.

Committee members questioned the government's failure to ensure an appropriate public return from an asset of such magnitude, stressing that institutional autonomy could not exempt the club from accountability for its occupation and use of state land.

Appearing before the committee alongside members of the club's management, Chairman Salman Siddique acknowledged the concerns raised by the lawmakers and expressed willingness to provide the relevant record and cooperate in the inquiry.

He said he was himself surprised by the nominal annual rent, particularly in view of the extent of the land occupied by the club and its improved financial position.

Comparing the club's present circumstances with the financial constraints it had faced during the 1990s, he said the annual rent should be at least Rs10 million.

The members said the acknowledgment had reinforced the need to determine why successive government authorities had allowed the arrangement to continue without scrutiny.

They stressed that the responsibility for protecting public assets rested with the relevant government institutions, which were required to enforce lease conditions and ensure accountability.

content:
Brazilian experts identify multiple crop diseases in belt as yields slashed by up to 70%

A wave of crop diseases has dealt a severe blow to sugarcane cultivation in Shaheed Benazirabad and adjoining areas, with Brazilian agricultural experts warning that infestations could cut per-acre yields by as much as 70%, prompting urgent calls for modern farming practices to prevent further losses.

A team of Brazilian agricultural specialists has arrived in Nawabshah at the invitation of a private sugar mill to assess the damage and advise growers on protecting their crops. Led by agricultural expert Dr William Burnsquist, the team visited severely affected sugarcane fields in Qazi Ahmed, Daulatpur and Shahpur Jehania, as well as surrounding areas.

During field inspections, the experts examined diseased crops and provided farmers with on-site guidance on modern techniques and preventive measures to contain the spread of infections.

According to the Brazilian specialists, sugarcane crops in the region are being affected by several serious diseases, including red rot, grassy shoot disease, Echinochloa grass infestation and shoot borer damage.

The reported damage has raised alarm among local growers, who are already facing substantial financial losses as the diseases threaten one of the area's key cash crops.

The experts urged farmers to move away from traditional cultivation methods and adopt modern agricultural practices, improved crop management and timely preventive measures to minimise damage and restore productivity.

title: LPG prices hit Rs580/kg amid gas shortages
author: Our Correspondent
summary: Daily demand exceeds 50 tonnes as residents turn to LPG; women protest prolonged gas outages
content:
Daily demand exceeds 50 tonnes as residents turn to LPG; women protest prolonged gas outages

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices in Hyderabad have surged to Rs580 per kilogram amid persistent natural gas shortages, with consumers forced to pay nearly twice the official rate as rising demand and alleged profiteering fuel black marketing.

The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has fixed the price of domestic LPG at Rs279.34 per kilogram for the current month. However, retailers across the city are charging between Rs550 and Rs580 per kilogram, adding to the financial burden on households already struggling with prolonged gas outages.

The city's daily LPG demand has exceeded 50 tonnes as residents increasingly turn to the alternative fuel for cooking amid an unreliable supply from Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC). The situation has also triggered frequent arguments between consumers and shopkeepers over prices.

Abdul Qadir, general secretary of the LPG Union Association Hyderabad, alleged that OGRA-registered producers were supplying LPG to retailers at Rs520 per kilogram or higher, leaving shopkeepers to add transportation and other expenses to the final price.

"OGRA has fixed the price after including all applicable taxes, but producers themselves are supplying LPG at rates far above the notified price," Qadir told The Express Tribune.

He said the association had repeatedly lodged complaints with OGRA and registered LPG companies, but the prices remained unchanged. He added that the divisional commissioner and deputy commissioner of Hyderabad had also been informed, while meetings with representatives of LPG plants had been held to discuss the issue.

Qadir said five LPG plants operated in the wider Hyderabad-Jamshoro area, including three in Hyderabad, one in Jamshoro and one in Kotri. He maintained that a reduction in government taxes could help bring prices down.

Around 250 shops across Hyderabad district sell LPG, which is increasingly being used not only by households but also by rickshaws, Qingqi rickshaws, mini-taxis, Suzuki vehicles, hotels, restaurants and tea stalls. The rising cost of the fuel has also contributed to higher prices of food items, according to the report.

SSGC's gas supply schedule has further compounded the crisis. Domestic consumers receive gas for three hours at a time, three times a day, while low pressure and delays in the restoration of supply continue to disrupt household routines. Residents say that during the morning, evening and night supply windows, air often flows through pipelines for the first 15 to 20 minutes before gas becomes available.

Separately, women residents of Amani Shah Colony in Latifabad, Unit 11, staged a protest at Khuda Hafiz Board Chari against prolonged gas shortages, suspending traffic and chanting slogans against SSGC management.

title: City fish harbour gets security overhaul
author: Our Correspondent
summary: CM orders dedicated police station, RFID tracking, crackdown on export irregularities
content:
CM orders dedicated police station, RFID tracking, crackdown on export irregularities

With a deadly shooting exposing the fault lines at Karachi Fish Harbour, the Sindh government has ordered a sweeping security overhaul at the province's key seafood hub, where 20,000 people enter daily and unchecked commercial activity, congestion and weak access controls have raised serious law-and-order concerns.

Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Wednesday directed Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar to strengthen security and pursue the establishment of a dedicated police station at the harbour in consultation with the Fisheries Department.

Chairing a meeting at his office, CM Shah also ordered mandatory registration of all harbour users, the introduction of RFID-based identification cards and an upgrade of the existing database to improve access control and monitoring.

The meeting reviewed law and order, infrastructure deficiencies, utility connections, fish auction arrangements, the management of the Fishermen Cooperative Society and the regulation of seafood exports.

Officials informed the meeting that the harbour operates round the clock, accommodating fishermen, auction agents, vendors, labourers, transporters, seafood processors, ice dealers and foreign nationals. The large volume of activity, coupled with inadequate security personnel, has placed pressure on the facility's security and infrastructure.

The briefing cited a firing incident on September 8, reportedly triggered by a dispute over placing fish on a road, in which one person was killed and six others injured.

CM Shah directed officials to ensure that fish unloading, auctions and related commercial activities take place only in designated areas, keeping roads and access routes clear.

The chief minister ordered the completion of registration records and the integration of the harbour's management information system with the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) verification system, a mobile application and the Crime Record Management System.

The meeting was informed that the Karachi Fisheries Harbour Authority (KFHA) had registered 5,196 boats and issued 170,000 computerised cards to harbour users since 2001, including 155,000 crew cards. Officials were also directed to obtain missing registration details of people associated with the Fishermen Cooperative Society.

Established by the federal government in 1959 over 84 acres, the harbour was transferred to Sindh in 1974 after fisheries came under provincial jurisdiction. The KFHA was established in 1984 to oversee its management and rehabilitation.

The meeting also examined a Rs5.7 million electricity bill disputed by the Fishermen Cooperative Society following the removal of a meter. CM Shah directed the fisheries minister to resolve the matter and arrange a separate electricity connection. A separate water connection was also ordered to meet operational needs and support compliance with European Union requirements for seafood exports. Officials were asked to examine the restoration of the harbour's cold storage facility, while illegal encroachments in designated areas used by ice dealers were ordered to be removed.

The society proposed establishing a new auction hall at K-6, removing hotels and allocating dedicated spaces for fish vendors. The fisheries minister was directed to examine the proposals to reduce congestion and prevent disputes over the use of roads and common areas.

CM Shah also called for tighter monitoring of seafood exporters operating outside the harbour, citing concerns over alleged illegal fish warehouses, revenue losses and discrepancies between recorded weights and export declarations. Officials were directed to improve documentation and traceability and take action under applicable laws.

The meeting reviewed progress on a Rs2.779 billion rehabilitation scheme for the harbour's external services. Of the total cost, Rs1.426 billion has been spent, while Rs311 million has been allocated for the current fiscal year, of which Rs46.65 million has been released.

While road works are 90% complete, the CCTV system is only 5% complete. Several other components, including the fixed jetty and floating pontoons, have yet to record physical progress.

CM Shah directed the fisheries department to remove bottlenecks and accelerate pending works, particularly CCTV surveillance, street lighting and the security control room.

title: Sheesha cafés face indefinite closure
author: Our Correspondent
summary: CJ Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar criticises prolonged delay in framing the rules
content:
CJ Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar criticises prolonged delay in framing the rules

The federal government's failure to finalise regulations governing sheesha cafés despite repeated revisions and extensions has prompted the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to intervene, directing officials to complete the regulatory framework without unnecessary delay.

In its detailed written judgment, Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar observed that the Sheesha Rules 2023 had not been finalised despite the passage of considerable time.

The draft regulations had repeatedly been returned to the relevant ministry for revision by the Cabinet Committee for Legislative Cases.

The court noted that proceedings had been initiated because the regulatory framework remained incomplete despite repeated extensions and assurances given to it.

Observing that no specific rules and regulations governing sheesha cafés were currently in place, the IHC directed the relevant authorities to finalise the framework without unnecessary delay.

The court ruled that all sheesha cafés in Islamabad would remain closed until the regulations were framed, including establishments holding existing no-objection certificates (NOCs).

It ordered that previously issued certificates be treated as withdrawn.

The chief commissioner, deputy commissioner and Islamabad inspector general of police were directed to ensure implementation of the order.

The court also noted that an IHC order issued in 2022 concerning sheesha cafés had not been implemented. The Supreme Court had also issued directions to all provinces regarding sheesha cafés in a suo motu case in 2016.

Incorporating World Health Organisation guidelines into its judgment, the court observed that sheesha smoking exposes users to nicotine, carbon monoxide and other toxic substances that can cause cancer.

It further noted that tobacco smoke poses serious health risks to children and other vulnerable people in surrounding areas. Citing WHO reports, the judgment said sheesha smoking should be prohibited in enclosed public places and shopping malls, adding that passing smoke through water does not eliminate its toxic substances.

title: Islamabad LG polls set for Dec 20
author: Waqas Ahmed
summary: Nomination papers to be filed from Nov 2-6; final candidate list due on Nov 25
content:
Nomination papers to be filed from Nov 2-6; final candidate list due on Nov 25

Local government elections in the federal capital will be held on December 20, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) announced on Tuesday, issuing the election schedule along with strict instructions to ensure a transparent and impartial electoral process.

According to the schedule, nomination papers will be available from October 30 and may be filed from November 2 to 6. The list of candidates will be published on November 7, while scrutiny of nomination papers will take place from November 9 to 13.

Appeals against decisions on nomination papers may be filed from November 14 to 18, with decisions to be announced from November 19 to 23. The final list of candidates will be displayed on November 25, followed by the allotment of election symbols on November 26.

Polling will take place from 8am to 4pm on December 20, and the ECP said it will announce election results between December 21 and 24.

The commission has prohibited the use of government resources for election campaigning. The ECP will also bar transfers and postings of government officers after the schedule is announced, and public servants will not be permitted to take leave without the ECP's approval.

The President, Prime Minister, federal ministers and governors will not be allowed to campaign in the local government elections. However, members of Parliament, senators and local government representatives may participate in campaigning.

The ECP warned that legal action would be taken against government officers found influencing election results and public office-holders violating electoral laws. It also directed that election offices remain open during public holidays and that election-related activities be conducted during official working hours, with strict compliance with the code of conduct.

The commission said all relevant institutions and officials must follow its instructions to ensure that the electoral process is completed transparently, fairly and in accordance with the law.

Earlier, the ECP had decided to hold the Islamabad local government elections under the 2015 local government law and ordered the immediate issuance of the schedule.

Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja observed that holding local government elections was a constitutional obligation, but the federal government had failed to provide the new local government law and relevant rules.

The ECP said delimitation had been carried out six times and election schedules issued four times in Islamabad. It maintained that holding the elections under the 2015 law would not affect the existing delimitation.

title: Courts paralysed after judge assault
author: Qaiser Shirazi
summary: Lawyers, clerks and judicial staff staged separate protests
content:
Lawyers, clerks and judicial staff staged separate protests

Judicial proceedings at Rawalpindi's Judicial Complex and district courts were disrupted on Tuesday as lawyers, their clerks and judicial staff staged separate protests following an alleged attack on Civil Judge Malik Ali Miran inside his chamber.

On the appeal of the District Bar Association, lawyers observed a complete strike and boycotted court proceedings, while judicial staff also stopped work in protest over the incident.

The protests prompted heightened security at the Judicial Complex and the old district courts. Additional police personnel were deployed to deal with any possible confrontation between the two sides.

Visitors were allowed into the Judicial Complex only after strict checking at the main entrances.

Judicial staff and lawyers' clerks and assistants held separate rallies inside the Judicial Complex. Judicial staff chanted slogans against terrorism and hooliganism, while lawyers' clerks protested against what they described as intimidation and the registration of a false case.

The Bar Clerks Association expressed full support for the lawyers and the District Bar Association, condemning the terrorism-related case as retaliatory and fabricated. It demanded the withdrawal of the FIR and warned that daily protests would continue if the case was not withdrawn.

An FIR was registered against seven lawyers, including Aslam Khan Niazi, on the complaint of the judge's reader, Tahir Abbas Shah. The case includes charges relating to terrorism, assault and attempted murder. No lawyer had been arrested, and the FIR was sealed.

District Bar Association President Malik Sajid Mahmood and Secretary Qamarul Haq Niazi said the arrest of any lawyer would have serious consequences, declaring that the arrest of a lawyer was a red line for the bar.

They said the lawyers were willing to negotiate and resolve the matter through dialogue but would not be blackmailed. They also called on judges to correct their conduct.

Judges remained silent publicly but reportedly observed an unofficial strike, remaining in their chambers instead of hearing cases.

On their instructions, court staff wore black armbands and held a protest rally inside the Judicial Complex, raising slogans over the incident.

Court staff returned to their duties in courtrooms after 1pm, before the end of the court day, and the process for filing new cases was reopened.

However, hearings in cases scheduled for the morning had largely been adjourned, with fresh dates given to litigants. The courts had become largely empty of visitors after 9.30am.

The authorised authority of the Lahore High Court also took notice of the incident. During high-level consultations between the bar and the bench, it was decided that the matter would be resolved through dialogue.

According to the complainant, during court hours, Aslam Niazi and Muhammad Farooq Aslam attempted to enter the judge's chamber along with other lawyers. When they were stopped, they allegedly used abusive language, engaged in physical altercations and forced their way inside. Court staff subsequently entered the chamber as well.

The FIR alleges that Aslam Niazi verbally abused the civil judge and loudly questioned why an application against him had been accepted.

The judge reportedly replied that he had decided the application in accordance with the law and that an appeal could be filed against the decision.

The complainant alleged that Aslam Niazi then threatened the judge with serious consequences and struck him on the head with a glass, hitting him above the left eye.

title: Macron rebukes foreign leaders over unrest rhetoric
author: AFP
summary: Far-right politicians blame immigrants for French protests
content:
Far-right politicians blame immigrants for French protests

Far-right politicians around the world have blamed immigration for France's recent riots, exploiting the unrest ahead of crucial elections despite there being no established link between the violence and immigration.

The riots, which erupted from protests over the cost of living, have become a talking point for politicians in the United States, Spain and Israel, where populist leaders face electoral tests. French President Emmanuel Macron, however, appeared to criticise the foreign leaders.

US President Donald Trump claimed France had been "conquered, looted and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists and communists". Spain's far-right Vox leader Santiago Abascal warned of "Islamo-leftism", while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described France as facing an "invasion".

Marine Le Pen, France's far-right presidential candidate who is leading polls for next year's election, has blaming "decades of anarchic immigration" for the country's problems. Macron condemned "people who campaign at France's expense" and the "stupid comments by many, including foreign leaders".

Political scientist Pascal Perrineau said people from immigrant backgrounds were among those involved in the unrest, but represented only one section of a diverse crowd that also included students, revolutionary activists and radical "black bloc" protesters.

The demonstrations initially involved students complaining about poor conditions at school before widening into broader anger over inflation and the cost of living. Perrineau warned that France's presidential election campaign could become "extremely agitated" amid years of recurring protests and deep social divisions.

title: Brazil rivals seek disqualification of each other

content:
Brazil's presidential rivals Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro have moved to disqualify each other over allegations of social media misconduct, escalating tensions ahead of Sunday's runoff election.

Lula's campaign said it would ask the country's top electoral court on Wednesday to disqualify Bolsonaro over alleged election interference by Meta, the owner of Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram. Bolsonaro's team filed its own complaint on Tuesday, accusing the incumbent of "abuse of power" through the mass dissemination of government posts on WhatsApp during the campaign.

The legal battle follows allegations by Lula's campaign that Meta manipulated its algorithms to suppress his online content and improve Bolsonaro's chances. The court on Monday ordered the company to demonstrate within 24 hours that it was treating both campaigns equally, threatening a daily fine of around $200,000 for non-compliance.

Meta said on Tuesday it had implemented measures to comply with the order. The company has denied favouring either candidate, although it acknowledged that some of Lula's campaign advertisements had been mistakenly deactivated because of technical errors.

Lula's campaign has also alleged inconsistencies in WhatsApp's artificial intelligence tool, claiming that election-related content supporting the president was restricted while Bolsonaro-related material remained unaffected.

Meta said it had removed 720 posts containing AI-generated material that lacked proper labelling. It also restricted political advertising on its platforms to candidates and parties registered with the electoral court.

The dispute comes as the candidates prepare for a closely contested second round. Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, secured 47% of the vote in the first round earlier this month, compared with Lula's 45%. Opinion polls indicate a technical tie ahead of Sunday's vote.

content:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged Republicans to defy unfavourable polling and deliver strong results in the November 3 midterm elections, rallying supporters in North Carolina, where his party faces a difficult Senate contest.

Trump's second visit to the state in as many months came as his approval rating fell to 31%, its lowest level across his two terms, according to a Reuters/Ipsos survey. "I think you're gonna see some amazing results," Trump told hundreds of supporters, dismissing polls as inaccurate and urging Republicans to turn out.

Rising fuel prices and dissatisfaction with his handling of the economy have added to Republican concerns. The Senate Leadership Fund, a major Republican campaign group, has withdrawn its spending from the state amid Republican Michael Whatley's poor polling.

Trump announced prospective investments in North Carolina, including a claimed $1.5 billion Defence Department investment in semiconductor production, but provided no details.

title: Putin agrees to resume US-mediated Ukraine talks
author: Reuters
summary:
Trilateral negotiations could begin in 
Abu Dhabi after US midterms
content:
Trilateral negotiations could begin in 
Abu Dhabi after US midterms

Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace negotiations with Ukraine as early as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, following a nearly three-hour meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.

The proposed trilateral talks, to be held at a technical level, could take place in Abu Dhabi on or after November 10, with discussions focusing on guarantees for Russia's and Ukraine's security after the war ends, Kremlin officials said.

The meeting marked Witkoff's ninth in-person encounter with Putin and came amid growing concerns in Kyiv and among its allies over Washington's commitment to Ukraine. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran.

The Kremlin said the discussions were less encouraging about the outcome of Witkoff's earlier meeting in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Nordic leaders and European and NATO representatives. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the proposals presented by Ukraine did not satisfy Moscow.

Putin used the meeting to offer assistance to Washington in dealing with Iran, saying a nuclear agreement with Tehran was both possible and necessary. He also offered to supply large quantities of fertiliser to help American farmers.

The Kremlin said the possibility of a meeting in China next month involving Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed, with Beijing reportedly preparing for the proposed encounter.

Despite the renewed diplomatic push, Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on the terms of a settlement. Putin has maintained demands for full Russian control of Ukraine's Donetsk region, Kyiv's exclusion from NATO and a comprehensive peace agreement rather than a temporary ceasefire.

Witkoff said he had brought documents containing ideas for a potential settlement for Putin to review. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, also conveyed proposals during the meeting remotely.

Meanwhile, tensions between Washington and Kyiv have persisted over intelligence sharing and Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite system. Zelenskiy said discussions in Oslo had produced an agreement to resolve those concerns, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that Washington had withdrawn Ukraine's access to Starlink.

title: Athens blast injures four
author: Reuters
content:
Two police officers and two members of the public were injured in an explosion at a building in central Athens on Wednesday, Greek police said.

The blast occurred in the Kolonos area when officers inspected a backpack suspected of containing drugs, a police official said. Police had earlier received calls from a resident and the building manager reporting suspected drugs at the entrance.

The explosion went off as officers examined the backpack and may have been remotely activated, a second police official said. Parts of an explosive device were later found at the scene.

All four injured people were taken away in ambulances, police said. The building manager was among those hurt in the blast. Police are not treating the incident as a terrorist act, an official said. The homicide unit is leading the investigation.
